item.title: Website owners thumb their noses at EU privacy rules, researcher finds
item.description: Privacy? What privacy? The 100 most-visited English-language sites are flouting European data protection laws on a massive scale, according to a privacy researcher's investigation. Forensic data analysis , published by Alexander Hanff, an attorney, computer scientist, and occasional contributor to The Register , with the support of SOMI (Stichting Onderzoek Marktinformatie), a Netherlands-based privacy group, details the dubious data flow. From October 1 to 3, 2026, Hanff took a clean Google Chrome browser profile and measured what happens when the browser loads the 100 most visited English-language websites for five minutes, without any consent banner interaction. At these 100 sites, visits were made to 265 pages – the home page, the privacy page, and the cookie notice when available – which resulted in 518,770 privacy events without any consent. All 100 sites produced what the report characterizes as Tier 1 events – interception, exfiltration, or high-entropy fingerprinting (a total of 14,675). Tier 2 consists of storage on the device, capturing device characteristics, and script loads without consent (284,463 events recorded). Tier 3 includes protocol mechanisms and passive reads used for tracking (219,632 events). The median website triggered 2,695 events, for a total of 28,695 events deemed high or critical. And 92.4 percent of the servers contacted during this process were on networks outside the European Economic Area (EEA). Most of these servers – 1,247 out of 1,400 – were in the US, and 1,034 belonged to third-parties. The EU General Data Protection Regulation governs the transfer of personal data outside the EEA. The EU allows data transfers to the US for organizations participating in the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. Beyond that, according to Hanff and SOMI, a valid legal mechanism like a contract must be in place or the transfer may fail to meet GDPR or the ePrivacy Directive. In some cases, California Penal Code section 631 (interception) and section 502 (computer access) may also be relevant. On these 100 websites, there were 89,437 fingerprinting events, 1,492 cookies set without consent, 7,456 scripts loaded from other origins, 18 websites implementing CNAME cloaking, and 37 websites delivering code to use the browser's built-in AI interfaces. The privacy and cookie notices on these websites imposed a median reading time requirement of 28 minutes and none fully matched what their pages did. Among the sites' consent banners, 115 out of 165 used dark patterns, like steering visitors with emotional language about a "safer" or "better" experience, or "we care about your privacy." The report, released in conjunction with a presentation at the Field Talk conference , also calculates the estimated environmental impact to load all this third-party content on websites without consent: 1,271,444 kWh per year, or enough to power 353 homes in Europe at 3.6 MWh per home annually. In some cases, California Penal Code section 631 (interception) and section 502 (computer access) may also be relevant. On these 100 websites, there were 89,437 fingerprinting events, 1,492 cookies set without consent, 7,456 scripts loaded from other origins, 18 websites implementing CNAME cloaking, and 37 websites delivering code to use the browser's built-in AI interfaces. Hanff in an email told The Register that he would be shocked if these findings fail to get the attention of lawmakers and regulators in the EU, UK, and US, given plans to file privacy complaints with relevant authorities. "Complaints will be filed against all of them and the EU supervisory authorities have a legal obligation to investigate them all – so we will have to wait and see," he said. "One of the things we are discussing with SOMI is mass claims under the EU’s Representative Actions Directive but we are hoping that the industry and the regulators do the right thing so we don’t have to file lawsuits – again we will have to wait and see." ®

item.title: Get ready for a nationwide emergency alert test at 2:20PM ET today
item.description: Radio and TV broadcasts will be interrupted for about one minute at 2:20PM ET on Tuesday while FEMA and the FCC test the country's Emergency Alert System. Unlike recent communications outages , this is a planned interruption that FEMA is required to run every three years. FEMA says today's test includes radio and television broadcasters, cable systems, satellite radio and television providers, and wireline video providers. This test doesn't include phones. You'll hear high-pitched alert tones and the following test message: "This is a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System, issued by the Federal Emergency Management Agency. This is … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Senate chief whip, Monguno, others escape suspected Boko Haram attack in Borno
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The Senate Chief Whip and Senator representing Borno North, Mohammed Tahir Monguno, alongside some All Progressives Congress (APC) stalwarts, have escaped Boko Haram’s attempted attack in the Kukawa Local Government Area of the state. Sources said Monguno and a former Governor Senator Maina Maaji Lawan, among others, stormed Kukawa in continuation of their 2027 campaign tour. Earlier, Monguno had joined Governor Babagana Zulum at the official launch of the campaign in Monguno town last Sunday, before the governor disengaged on Monday from Monguno back to Maiduguri via a helicopter, while some of his entourage arrived in Maiduguri the same day by road. Sources said some politicians, including the Senate Chief Whip, proceeded from Monguno to Kukawa to canvass for votes, in which the terrorists attempted to dislodge the community. It was also gathered that, based on intelligence, troops of Operation Hadin Kai swung into action and foiled the attempted attacks by terrorists on the campaign entourage. According to reports by Yerwa News Express, a local online media outlet said, “The terrorists fired three mortar bombs toward Kukawa on Monday while Mr Monguno, former Borno State Governor Maina Maaji Lawan, and other political figures were in the town for campaign activities. “Local sources had earlier reported threats by the terrorists to disrupt the campaign, prompting heightened security measures. “Troops of Operation Hadin Kai detected the movement of the terrorists around Kukawa and swiftly responded, preventing them from carrying out the attack. “The campaign team subsequently returned safely to Monguno without any casualties. “The terrorists reportedly made further attempts to attack the town throughout the night but were prevented from gaining access.” In a related development, troops foiled another attempted attack on Kekeno village in the early hours of Tuesday, November 17, 2026. “At about 1:20 a.m., alert troops spotted suspicious movements by suspected terrorists travelling on foot from the general area of Barwati toward Kekeno village. “The troops immediately advanced toward the suspected terrorists and engaged them with heavy gunfire. “Unable to withstand the troops’ firepower, the terrorists reportedly fled into the surrounding bush. “The military said follow-up operations are ongoing in the area to track down the fleeing terrorists. “It added that the situation remained calm, with troops maintaining heightened surveillance.” Sources and Yerwa Express News reported. Due to a lack of telecommunication networks in the zone, the Senate Chief Whip’s phone number was not available at the time our correspondent dialled to confirm the incident. The post Senate chief whip, Monguno, others escape suspected Boko Haram attack in Borno appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: The Fire TV Stick 4K Plus is on sale for less than Amazon’s entry-level streamer
item.description: Amazon no longer considers the midrange Fire TV Stick 4K Plus as part of its official lineup following the launch of it latest Fire TV Stick 4K, but that doesn’t mean the streaming device isn’t still good value. In fact, it’s an even more attractive option now that it’s dropped to $29.99 ($40 off) at Amazon and Best Buy in the run-up to Black Friday. That’s just $5 shy of its lowest price to date, rendering it cheaper than both the entry-level Fire TV Stick HD and its new midrange replacement, the Fire TV Stick 4K . Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K Plus Where to Buy: $69.99 $29.99 at Amazon $69.99 $29.99 at Best Buy The Fire TV Stick 4K Plus still offers a good balance of price and performance. Unlike its replacement, it supports both Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, delivering more vibrant colors, better contrast, and immersive audio with compatible TVs and speakers. It does require a separate power adapter, though, whereas the newer model can draw power directly from your TV’s USB port. You also don’t get as much storage here as with the high-end Fire TV Stick 4K Max , though 8GB should be plenty for streaming apps like Netflix and Disney Plus. The Plus model also supports Amazon’s redesigned Fire TV interface, which my colleague John Higgins found to be an impressive update . It makes it easier to browse different content categories and pin your favorite apps for quick access. Thanks to Alexa Plus support, you can also press the voice button on the included Alexa Voice Remote to find something to watch, control compatible smart home devices like lights and thermostats, check sports scores, and more without getting off your couch. Just don’t expect a customizable shortcut button, as that’s exclusive to the latest Fire TV Remote. item.title: What we learned from the Jets' loss to the Bills in Week 10
item.description: The New York Jets were once again embarrassed on Sunday . They were blown out 31-12 by their AFC East rival Buffalo Bills in Week 10 . Head coach Aaron Glenn is now 0-9 all-time in divisional contests. It marked the Jets' fifth-consecutive defeat, and third straight where they've allowed the opposing offense to score 30+ points. Glenn's defense isn't meeting expectations. The hapless Jets are 2-8. With that, Jets Wire has identified three notable happenings from Sunday's latest setback. Braelon Allen should see more carries The workload between Breece Hall and Braelon Allen was more even at running back this week . Hall rushed for a team-high 41 yards, but only averaged 3.7 yards per attempt on 11 carries. Meanwhile, Allen rushed for 5.0 YPC, gaining 40 yards on eight carries. With Hall still coming back from injury, the workload should be an even split. Why can't Omar Cooper Jr. and Kenyon Sadiq be productive? Jets rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. exited Sunday's defeat with an ankle injury . It occcurred on the first offensive series of the game. It was another example of the Jets' struggles to get Cooper and Kenyon Sadiq productive in the same game. Sadiq had three receiving yards after having 49 last weekend. Rookie QB Cade Klubnik isn't ready Jets starting QB Geno Smith also exited with an injury . Rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik replaced him. Klubnik completed 11-of-20 passing attempts for 137 yards, zero touchdowns, and an interception. He won't prevent the Jets from drafting a QB in April. This article originally appeared on Jets Wire: What we learned from the Jets' loss to the Bills in Week 10

item.title: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph expected to return against Buccaneers
item.description: Kerby Joseph is closing in on playing his first game in more than 13 months. Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell said in his weekly interview Tuesday, Nov. 17, on 97.1 The Ticket (WXYT-FM) that, barring any setbacks, the Lions will activate Joseph this week off the physically unable to perform list with an eye on having him make his season debut Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Joseph has not played since last Oct. 12 because of a cartilage condition in his knee. "I mean, barring anything else here negatively, which there hasn’t been any, he’s progressed nicely here," Campbell said. "The plan would be to get him going this week. Get him going and get him into Tampa Bay and let him play." Campbell did specify how the Lions plan to manage Joseph's snaps against the Bucs and with a quick turnaround to next week's Thanksgiving game against the Chicago Bears . Joseph returned to practice Oct. 26 and took part in position drills for a week before graduating to scout-team duties and team drills last week. INSIDE THE LIONS: Where do Lions turn without Aidan Hutchinson? This time, they're ready His return comes at a time when the Lions are getting good play from their secondary and have depth at safety after the return of Brian Branch and the addition of Andre Cisco , but lost top pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson to a season-ending knee injury. Chuck Clark has started every game at safety, and Branch has joined him in the lineup since he came back from the torn Achilles tendon he suffered last year. Campbell said the Lions likely will be without starting center Cade Mays for another week because of a sprained ankle. Juice Scruggs has played well while starting seven games at center this season. "I don’t see Cade being ready this week," Campbell said. "There’s a chance, but I don’t – I’m not putting all my eggs in that basket. And Juice has been doing a nice job for us. He’s playing really good football. That whole O-line played dang good football the other day." Dave Birkett covers the Lions for the Detroit Free Press. Contact him at dbirkett@freepress.com . Follow him on Bluesky , X and Instagram at @davebirkett. This article originally appeared on Detroit Free Press: Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph expected to return against Buccaneers

item.title: Arch Manning Commits To Senior Day As NFL Draft Clock Ticks
item.description: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images Arch Manning is not hiding from the moment. The Texas quarterback announced Monday that he will participate in the Senior Day ceremonies before the Longhorns face Arkansas on Saturday. The decision secures his place in the pregame tradition, even if he chooses to return to Austin for another season. It does not, however, answer the biggest question surrounding his future: Is this his final college season, or will he put off the NFL Draft for another year? Manning’s stance is clear, even if his future remains a mystery. He told reporters, “I’m a senior, so I’m doing it,” regarding the specific Senior Day events, per reports. The 20-year-old has one season of eligibility left after this year, meaning he could return to Texas in 2027 if he skips the draft. Texas is 8-2 and was ranked No. 6 in the College Football Playoff committee’s most recent rankings, released November 10. The Longhorns have since added a dramatic victory over LSU and remain in contention for a playoff berth. The Quarterback’s Growing Pains A roller-coaster season defined Manning’s time so far. After a thrilling 24-23 September win against Ohio State that earned Texas the No. 1 ranking, the team subsequently dropped two of their following four contests to Florida and Oklahoma. Those losses sparked questions about whether he needed another year to develop his skills. The Longhorns have since won four straight games, including three against ranked opponents like Ole Miss, Missouri, and LSU. This run has restored the buzz around the program and put Manning back in the spotlight. His statistics show a season of considerable progress, but also some costly mistakes. Manning has completed 64.7 percent of his passes for 2,198 yards, 19 touchdowns and 10 interceptions. His three-interception performance against LSU nearly cost Texas the game, but he delivered when it mattered most, throwing the winning touchdown with three seconds remaining. Despite the ups and downs, he insists his college career has “been great.” He told reporters, “I feel like I’ve grown a lot as a person and a player,” according to the New York Post . The pressure to perform is high, but he seems ready to handle it. One Week At A Time The draft question looms large, but Manning refuses to let it distract him. He is focused entirely on the upcoming game against Arkansas rather than what happens after the season ends. “I’ve enjoyed my time, but I’m just focused on this week, winning this week. I’m not really thinking about the future right now,” Manning said, per the New York Post . This mindset keeps the team united and avoids the drama that often plagues senior quarterbacks. The Longhorns still have a shot to host a College Football Playoff game, which would be the perfect stage for a potential final college performance. Whether he leaves for the NFL or stays for another year, the path is set for a big finish.

item.title: AEW’s Adam Copeland reportedly fought a bear, and won
item.description: AEW’s Adam Copeland reportedly fought a bear, and won appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . From acting to pro-wrestling and now even fighting bears, is there anything AEW’s Adam Copeland can’t do? Apparently not. Just a few hours after wrestling at AEW Full Gear against Kazuchika Okada, news came out that Copeland was in a real-life fight with a bear. While Copeland failed to defeat Okada for the AEW International title, the reason for it now might be clear. Bear fights do take a toll, and that was evident after Copeland allegedly defeated one. The Wrestling Observer recently reported that Copeland was in a fight with a bear and apparently, he won, too. As per the report, Copeland was walking with his dogs when he saw a mother bear and her cubs walking toward him. Copeland knew that he had to make himself look bigger to scare the bear, but he was unable to do so because of the dog’s leash in his hands. Instead, without much time to react, Copeland decided to hit the bear under its chin with his shin. The bear was stunned and immediately left the scene. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Copeland, 53, is a former multi-time WWE Champion and even held a couple of titles in AEW. However, following his match at AEW All Out 2026, Copeland announced his decision to retire in 2027. Following his loss to Okada, Copeland was interviewed by Mick Foley. Copeland claimed that he needed to get a few answers and now believes he received them after his Full Gear match. However, the WWE Hall of Famer did not elaborate on what he meant. Planning on retiring in 2027, Copeland was once out of action for nine years and retired between 2011 and 2020. MORE AEW NEWS AEW star PAC’s wife pens emotional note months after his death

item.title: Aidan Hutchinson torn ACL: Detroit Lions’ worst fears confirmed
item.description: Sunday did not go as planned for the Detroit Lions . While the team was getting blown out by the New England Patriots in the NFL Munich game, star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson was injured while celebrating a Drake Maye sack . After the game, there was immediate fear that Hutchinson would miss extended time, and now those worst fears have been confirmed. According to NFL insider Ian Rapoport, Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL and will be out for the remainder of the season. MORE: NFC power rankings NFL Week 11: Kirk Cousins, Vikings climb as Packers slide While the Hutchinson news is a gut punch to the Lions, there is some good news for the team with have Kerby Joseph set to make his season debut , according to head coach Dan Campbell. That will at least provide a boost to the team’s secondary. Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell shakes hands with safety Kerby Joseph (31) during warm up at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri on Sunday, Oct. 12, 2025. item.title: Detroit Lions won't ban celebrations after Aidan Hutchinson injury
item.description: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell said he won’t have a longer discussion with players about what celebrations they should and shouldn’t do after Aidan Hutchinson suffered a season-ending torn ACL while jumping to celebrate a sack in last week’s win over the New England Patriots in Germany. “No. I don’t believe that,” Campbell said Tuesday, Nov. 17, in his weekly interview Tuesday, Nov. 17, on 97.1 The Ticket (WXYT-FM) . “I think what happened speaks for itself and we’re not talking to 8-year-olds here.” Campbell said he believes he tore his bicep one time as a player when he pumped his fist to celebrate a big play he made in a game. Campbell did not specify the game, but in his first season as a Lions tight end in 2006, he tore his triceps and played through the injury while wearing a brace on his arm. “I didn’t tell anybody,” Campbell said. “And I was just excited. I just pumped my arm. And so if you say, ‘Hey, don’t pump your arm next time, make sure you stay stoic.’ Man, this game is built off of emotion and if you have to contain yourself after a play is made – I’m not talking about in the moment, in the game, because you got to keep your head – then you’re really becoming something you’re not.” RELATED: Lions' concern high after Aidan Hutchinson injury: 'He's the heart and soul' Hutchinson hurt his right knee on the final offensive play of the opening series against the Patriots, when he dropped Maye for a 2-yard loss on third-and-13 that forced a field goal. Hutchinson leaped up from the sack and jumped in the air similar to how soccer star Cristiano Ronaldo celebrates goals. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye also suffered a serious ankle injury on the play. The injury was reminiscent of one former Lions linebacker Stephen Tulloch suffered while celebrating a sack in 2014. “Look, it’s one of those things, it happened, I hate it, I know he hates it,” Campbell said. “But I mean, the number of moves I’ve seen Hutch make and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one-leg lateral movements, lateral bounces, I’m just like, ‘It was one of those things, man.’ I hate it. But no, I think we all understand what it is and let’s be smart, but I’m not going to say − no, I’m not going to say nobody celebrates anymore.” With six sacks and 50 quarterback pressures in nine games, Hutchinson was in the midst of one his best seasons as a Lion, and Campbell said the team will take an “all hands on deck” approach to replacing the second-team All-Pro’s production. D.J. Wonnum will assume the role as the Lions’ top edge rusher, rookie second-round pick Derrick Moore should see more time as a backup, and Campbell said he’ll ask more of defensive tackles Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams and Skyler Gill-Howard, as well. item.content:encoded: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell said he won’t have a longer discussion with players about what celebrations they should and shouldn’t do after Aidan Hutchinson suffered a season-ending torn ACL while jumping to celebrate a sack in last week’s win over the New England Patriots in Germany. “No. I don’t believe that,” Campbell said Tuesday, Nov. 17, in his weekly interview Tuesday, Nov. 17, on 97.1 The Ticket (WXYT-FM) . “I think what happened speaks for itself and we’re not talking to 8-year-olds here.” Campbell said he believes he tore his bicep one time as a player when he pumped his fist to celebrate a big play he made in a game. Campbell did not specify the game, but in his first season as a Lions tight end in 2006, he tore his triceps and played through the injury while wearing a brace on his arm. “I didn’t tell anybody,” Campbell said. “And I was just excited. I just pumped my arm. And so if you say, ‘Hey, don’t pump your arm next time, make sure you stay stoic.’ Man, this game is built off of emotion and if you have to contain yourself after a play is made – I’m not talking about in the moment, in the game, because you got to keep your head – then you’re really becoming something you’re not.” RELATED: Lions' concern high after Aidan Hutchinson injury: 'He's the heart and soul' Hutchinson hurt his right knee on the final offensive play of the opening series against the Patriots, when he dropped Maye for a 2-yard loss on third-and-13 that forced a field goal. Hutchinson leaped up from the sack and jumped in the air similar to how soccer star Cristiano Ronaldo celebrates goals. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye also suffered a serious ankle injury on the play. The injury was reminiscent of one former Lions linebacker Stephen Tulloch suffered while celebrating a sack in 2014. “Look, it’s one of those things, it happened, I hate it, I know he hates it,” Campbell said. “But I mean, the number of moves I’ve seen Hutch make and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one-leg lateral movements, lateral bounces, I’m just like, ‘It was one of those things, man.’ I hate it. But no, I think we all understand what it is and let’s be smart, but I’m not going to say − no, I’m not going to say nobody celebrates anymore.” With six sacks and 50 quarterback pressures in nine games, Hutchinson was in the midst of one his best seasons as a Lion, and Campbell said the team will take an “all hands on deck” approach to replacing the second-team All-Pro’s production. D.J. Wonnum will assume the role as the Lions’ top edge rusher, rookie second-round pick Derrick Moore should see more time as a backup, and Campbell said he’ll ask more of defensive tackles Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams and Skyler Gill-Howard, as well. McNeill leads the Lions with 6½ sacks, Wonnum has six and Moore has four – all in the past two games – despite playing sparingly early in the year. “No different than we did with Jack [Campbell],” Dan Campbell said of how the Lions responded to Jack Campbell’s serious neck injury. “No different than what we did in ’24 [when Hutchinson broke his leg]. We’ll talk about this. I mean, the bottom line is this: We’re prepared to handle this storm, we are suited to handle this storm actually I think better than we were in ’24. That’s the good news.” Hutchinson broke the tibia and fibula in his left leg in an early-season game in 2024 against the Dallas Cowboys. The Lions finished that season 15-2, the best record in franchise history, but lost their first playoff game to the Washington Commanders. Last year, Hutchinson had a career-high 14½ sacks in his return from injury. “What a gut punch,” Campbell said. “He’s very much like Jack, he’s such a phenomenal player. This guy’s an impact player, but more importantly he’s an unbelievable teammate and he’s one of our captains. So it just, it stinks, man. It hits you, and I hate it for him. I hate it for him because he was on a heater, man. What a hell of a year he was having. He’s just improved every year and to come off the injury he had. But I also know this, that this guy will overcome this and he’ll come back better than he was, too. It’s just the way he is, it’s the way he’s wired and he’ll come out better than this.” Dave Birkett covers the Lions for the Detroit Free Press. Contact him at dbirkett@freepress.com . Follow him on Bluesky , X and Instagram at @davebirkett. This article originally appeared on Detroit Free Press: Detroit Lions won't ban celebrations after Aidan Hutchinson injury

item.title: All About the 2026 F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, From Top Drivers to Star-Studded Parties
item.description: Las Vegas Grand Prix 2025. Credit: Will Lester/MediaNews Group/Inland Valley Daily Bulletin via Getty NEED TO KNOW Here’s a complete guide to the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix The Formula 1 night race takes place on Saturday, Nov. 21 on the 3.8-mile Las Vegas Strip Circuit Sean Paul, Disclosure and Two Friends headline performances alongside free fan experiences across the Las Vegas Strip Buckle up! The 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix is just around the corner, and there’s plenty of high-octane thrills happening off the grid. Between star-studded parties and events, Sin City has much to offer in the lead-up to the big Formula 1 race on Saturday night, Nov. 21. Now entering its fourth year, F1’s modern street race will take place on a 3.8-mile (6.2 km) temporary street circuit known as the Las Vegas Strip Circuit, lit up by the city’s most iconic landmarks. Drivers competing will pass casinos and attractions such as the Sphere, the Bellagio and more. The Las Vegas Grand Prix is unique because of a stacked on-track schedule, not to mention the support series, like the F1 Academy finale. The paddock is also a who’s who during race weekend, with Formula 1 drivers and the A-List celebrities swarming the scene. Additionally, a standout lineup of musical performances with festival-like hospitality setups around the track is expected. Sean Paul, Disclosure, Two Friends, Shaggy, Natasha Bedingfield and more are slated to take the city’s stages. Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli already won the 2026 Formula 1 World Drivers’ Championship (and made history at age 20 as the youngest driver to clinch the title since Sebastian Vettel in 2010 at age 23), so the race for second and third place is on. Red Bull Racing’s Max Verstappen and Mercedes’ George Russell are among the drivers in contention. Now, scroll on for everything to know about the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix. What is the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix? Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix 2025. Credit: Alex Bierens de Haan/Getty The Las Vegas Grand Prix marks the 21st stop on the 2026 Formula 1 calendar held at the temporary Las Vegas Strip Circuit. Two stops remain after this race: The Qatar Grand Prix at the Lusail International Circuit on Nov. 29, and the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix at the Yas Marina Circuit on Dec. 6. When is the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix? Lando Norris of McLaren races in the 2025 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Credit: Wu Xiaoling/Xinhua via Getty The 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix takes place on Saturday, Nov. 21 at 8:00 p.m. local time. Practice 1 and Practice 2 take place on Thursday, Nov. 19. Practice 3 and Qualifying take place on Friday, Nov. 20. There is no sprint race at this stop. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! Who is racing in the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix? Lewis Hamilton (left); Kimi Antonelli (center); Max Verstappen (right). Credit: Clive Mason/Getty; Stephanie Tacy/NurPhoto via Getty; Kym Illman/Getty The 2026 Formula 1 season features 11 teams (an expansion from 10, due to Cadillac’s entry this year). Each team has two cars and 22 drivers on the grid. Below is a full breakdown of the teams and drivers expected for the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend this year: Alpine: Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto Aston Martin: Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll Audi (formerly Kick Sauber): Nico Hülkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto Cadillac: Valtteri Bottas and Sergio “Checo” Pérez Ferrari: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc Haas: Rafael Câmara and Oliver Bearman McLaren: Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris Mercedes: George Russell and Kimi Antonelli Racing Bulls: Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad Red Bull Racing: Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar Williams: Alex Albon and Carlos Sainz Who is performing at the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix? Sean Paul performs in July 2024. Credit: Simone Joyner/Getty There are several concerts taking place along the track at the Las Vegas Grand Prix this year. Attendees can expect a world-class entertainment lineup at the T-Mobile Stage in the T-Mobile Zone at Sphere, with Sean Paul, Disclosure and Two Friends set to headline three nights during race weekend. Set beneath the remarkable glow of Sphere’s Exosphere, the space transforms into a race week festival experience featuring live music, immersive fan activations and premium trackside views. Additional performances will include Natasha Bedingfield, Gorgon City, Ja Rule, Collect 200, DJ Mandy and more. What parties, events and pop-ups are at the F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix? Jay-Z and Beyonce arrive to the paddock at the 2025 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Credit: Alex Bierens de Haan/Getty If you don’t have a ticket to the race, no problem! There are numerous pop-ups and Formula 1 activations happening around The Strip to immerse fans in the action, including places to see the high-speed cars up close and shops to snag the newest merch. The Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team Las Vegas Fan Hub is headed to Las Vegas following the United States Grand Prix in Austin last month. It includes free entry, an F1 pitstop challenge, racing simulators, a show car, interactive team activations and team apparel. The Atlassian Williams F1 Team Fan Zone is activating in Sin City at the Brooklyn Bridge on the Las Vegas Strip inside the New York-New York Hotel & Casino. Open to the public with no ticket required, the pop-up features race car displays, racing simulators, merchandise and surprise team appearances throughout the week. The Venetian Resort , positioned on a corner turn of the track and facing 20% of the total course, houses the F1 Hub presented by American Express. Check out new collaborations with Etai LA, Greg Yuna and Off Season, along with designs from Disney, Bape, the Vegas Golden Knights and F1 Academy x Hello Kitty and Friends. The BWT Alpine Formula One Team is an official partner of The Venetian Resort, which also doubles as the ultimate fan destination with hands-on activities such as race simulators and the opportunity to get up close with an official team show car. The Wynn puts motorsport fans in the epicenter of race weekend action, from the Charles Leclerc-inspired Café LeClerc to Lewis Hamilton’s streetwear-inspired brand +44 pop-up at Encore Esplanade to Lando Norris’ Lando Clubhouse pop-up in the Awakening Theater lobby. item.title: WWE 'Raw': LA Knight joins Cody Rhodes and CM Punk for 'Survivor Series'
item.description: Cody Rhodes arrives on the red carpet at the 2026 ESPY Awards in New York City on July 15, 2026. Rhodes asked LA Knight to join his team for "Survivor Series: WarGames." Photo by John Angelillo/UPI Nov. 17 (UPI) -- LA Knight joined Cody Rhodes and CM Punk's Survivor Series team on WWE Raw . Rhodes and Punk are co-captains for Team USA heading into the Survivor Series: WarGames event where they will be taking on Rey Mysterio's Team Mexico. Team Mexico also already gathered brothers Penta and Rey Fenix for the match, along with Dragon Lee. Team USA also has newcomer Je'Von Evans as a member. Team Mexico and Team USA will battle it out in a traditional five vs. five Survivor Series match. Rhodes and Punk were confronted by The Miz on Monday who demanded to have a spot on Team USA. The Miz mentioned all of his career accolades and how he came up in WWE the same time as Rhodes and Punk did. Knight then arrived onto the scene and joined Team USA, much to The Miz's dismay. Knight then challenged The Miz to a match , with the winner able to compete for Team USA. Knight won the match after nailing The Miz with his Blunt Force Trauma maneuver. Afterwards, The Miz's protege Kit Wilson got involved, leading to Punk taking him out with a GTS followed by a Cross Rhodes by Rhodes. Both Team USA and Team Mexico have one more member that will be announced at a later date. Survivor Series: WarGames takes place in Houston on Nov. 28.

item.title: Infantino challenger Diallo: Football needs a more 'respectful voice'
item.description: FILE PHOTO - FIFA president Gianni Infantino is silhouetted as he walks past the World Cup trophy after addressing the 76th FIFA Congress in Vancouver. (is associated with: «Infantino challenger Diallo: Football needs a more 'respectful voice'») Darryl Dyck/Canadian Press via ZUMA Press/dpa FIFA presidential candidate Philippe Diallo says football's values have been "trampled underfoot" by incumbent Gianni Infantino as he set out his stall ahead of March's election. European governing body UEFA announced on Monday that French Football Federation (FFF) chief Diallo would be its candidate to try to stop Infantino winning a fourth term at the top of the global game. The FFF executive committee unanimously backed Diallo's bid on Tuesday. "I believe I have the experience, the convictions, the values," the 63-year-old told reporters, according to broadcaster RMC. "I want to win, because what is happening has shocked people and does not match the future of football." Infantino is being challenged after a series of controversies, including an aborted attempt to sell off part of the World Cup to an investment group linked to the family of US President Donald Trump. His closeness to Trump, and US forward Folarin Balogun's suspension being lifted at this year's World Cup, angered European football despite Infantino being Swiss and a former UEFA official. "In a democratic process, it is time for someone else to bring a more respectful voice to football," Diallo added. He said he had initially not seen himself as a candidate, but relented after his European colleagues insisted. "The values of our sport have been trampled underfoot. The trust placed in our organization and its president has been broken," Diallo said. "To remain true to my convictions, I could not avoid (the challenge)." There has also been contact with Japanese candidate Kozo Tashima. It is unclear if he will drop out. "If we want to succeed, we must pool our strength and ensure that everyone who shares this vision unites to win," Diallo remarked. UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin decided not to stand but is close to Diallo, who emerged as a candidate after former Arsenal coach and current FIFA functionary Arsène Wenger opted against running. Diallo continued: "There can no longer be a solitary form of leadership in which the major issues of football are decided without any transparency." Infantino took over FIFA in 2016 after an array of scandals beset football's governing body.

European governing body UEFA announced on Monday that French Football Federation (FFF) chief Diallo would be its candidate to try to stop Infantino winning a fourth term at the top of the global game. The FFF executive committee unanimously backed Diallo's bid on Tuesday. "I believe I have the experience, the convictions, the values," the 63-year-old told reporters, according to broadcaster RMC. "I want to win, because what is happening has shocked people and does not match the future of football." Infantino is being challenged after a series of controversies, including an aborted attempt to sell off part of the World Cup to an investment group linked to the family of US President Donald Trump. His closeness to Trump, and US forward Folarin Balogun's suspension being lifted at this year's World Cup, angered European football despite Infantino being Swiss and a former UEFA official. "In a democratic process, it is time for someone else to bring a more respectful voice to football," Diallo added. He said he had initially not seen himself as a candidate, but relented after his European colleagues insisted. "The values of our sport have been trampled underfoot. The trust placed in our organization and its president has been broken," Diallo said. "To remain true to my convictions, I could not avoid (the challenge)." There has also been contact with Japanese candidate Kozo Tashima. It is unclear if he will drop out. "If we want to succeed, we must pool our strength and ensure that everyone who shares this vision unites to win," Diallo remarked. UEFA president Aleksander Čeferin decided not to stand but is close to Diallo, who emerged as a candidate after former Arsenal coach and current FIFA functionary Arsène Wenger opted against running. Diallo continued: "There can no longer be a solitary form of leadership in which the major issues of football are decided without any transparency." Infantino took over FIFA in 2016 after an array of scandals beset football's governing body.

item.title: Linda Cohn dismantles ESPN president Burke Magnus over Troy Aikman contract debacle
item.description: Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images ESPN have been battling against the frosty on-screen relationship between Troy Aikman and Joe Buck amid the ongoing contract saga. Monday Night Football rolled through Baltimore this week, and it was clear to see that the ESPN duo’s relationship had not noticeably improved. Aikman’s future remains uncertain with the network as talks over a potential new deal have hit an impasse. Meanwhile, Buck is sitting up in the booth alongside his colleague of many years with a brand new six-year extension worth $108 million. Linda Cohn knows exactly what it is like to work for ESPN having ended her 34-year run with the network earlier this year, and she is disgusted with the manner in which Aikman has been treated. Linda Cohn tears apart ESPN over their handling of Troy Aikman ESPN are considering replacements for Aikman , with the likes of Drew Brees, Greg Olsen and even Peyton Manning being suggested. The former Dallas Cowboys QB has received a lot of praise from Cohn for remaining as professional as he has been amid ESPN’s handling of the situation. “ESPN just butchered this. Burke Magnus, he is in this role, and why did he think that you do one contract and leave the other one hanging in the breeze?” Cohn told Yahoo Sports. “I don’t really put this on Joe Buck. I put it all, and I said this on The Linda Cohn Show, I put it all on ESPN and how they bungled it. You brought it up, Jason: you just don’t do business this way. I don’t care if it’s Troy Aikman or the production assistant that works on First Take, you don’t treat people like this. You really don’t, yet they did, and they did this to Troy Aikman.” Cohn is a legend of ESPN having worked with the network for over three decades. Having departed the company earlier this year, she is now able to speak freely about her thoughts on Burke Magnus and how he is handling the situation surrounding Aikman. “He [Aikman] is such a professional. I don’t know how he is dealing with all this. Let’s think about that for a second: he has to look Joe Buck in the face. I don’t know how the relationship is now; it looks cold as ice right now, of course, over the last month,” she added. “To be able to stand there, be professional, and analyse a football game, and not only do the game for three and a half hours, but do everything that comes with that game (travel, meetings with coaches and players), it is just absolutely absurd.” Read more: Aqib Talib praises ‘exceptional’ QB who’s part of NFL team with a ‘Tom Brady-style offence’ ‘That’s huge’ – Rob Gronkowski so impressed by what he noticed Fernando Mendoza doing on debut Skip Bayless stunned by what Josh Allen has admitted to doing for the Bills

item.title: Yankees Reportedly Made Competitive Offer To Pitcher Who Left Bronx In 2025
item.description: Free agent pitcher Jonathan Loáisiga The New York Yankees have already re-signed Tim Hill and extended a qualifying offer to David Bednar. However, Brian Cashman is focused on adding more relievers. Jonathan Loáisiga has reportedly drawn interest from many teams this offseason, but according to NJ.com's Randy Miller , the Yankees have already made him an offer. "The Yankees have offered a contract to Loáisiga, a source close to the Nicaraguan right-hander told NJ.com," wrote Miller. "The Yankees’ offer is believed to be a one-year deal worth more than Loáisiga’s only other offer, one year for $5 million from the (Arizona) Diamondbacks." According to Miller, Loáisiga is looking for a three-year deal in the $18 million to $20 million range. Loáisiga had a great year for the Diamondbacks, posting a 2.42 ERA in 67 games. He spent eight seasons pitching for the Yankees before last season. The Yankees declined his option last offseason, and he signed a minor league deal with the Diamondbacks. He had a bounce-back year, and now it makes a ton of sense for the Yankees to bring him back. Bringing back Bednar should be one of the Yankees' top priorities, but adding an arm like Loáisiga is also important. The team needs arms that can work in high-leverage situations. Loáisiga reportedly also has interest from the Los Angeles Dodgers, New York Mets and Philadelphia Phillies. There is no guarantee that Loáisiga accepts the Yankees' offer. However, the familiarity in the Bronx could give the Yankees an edge. They have reportedly already surpassed his only other offer to this point. More MLB: Mets Meeting With Tarik Skubal Reportedly 'Went Very Well'

item.title: Giants Legend Headlines 2027 Hall Of Fame Ballot
item.description: San Francisco Giants president of baseball operations Buster Posey The BBWAA unveiled its 2027 Hall of Fame ballot on Monday. The ballot has 27 players, including 14 first-time candidates. Voting concludes Dec. 31 and results will be announced on Jan. 19. The newcomers are led by San Francisco Giants legend Buster Posey and former ace Jon Lester, both of whom won three World Series rings. A seven-time All-Star in his 12 MLB seasons, Posey spent his entire career with the Giants, leading them to a trio of championships in five years from 2010 to 2014. One of the best and most decorated catchers in baseball history, he won an NL Rookie of the Year award, an NL MVP award, a Gold Glove award and five Silver Slugger awards. Now San Francisco's president of baseball operations, Posey is the strongest first-time candidate on the ballot. Time will tell if he gets in right away as his contemporary, Joe Mauer, did in 2024. More MLB: Mets Meeting With Tarik Skubal Reportedly 'Went Very Well'

item.title: Chris Long says it’s so stupid what people are now saying about Mike Vrabel with the Patriots
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images Chris Long was not a fan of people calling out Mike Vrabel for drinking beer before the New England Patriots’ game against the Detroit Lions on Sunday. A video of Vrabel drinking from a frosted stein at a Munich beer hall made the rounds on the internet. He visited Augustiner Stammhaus, which is a designated Patriots fan pub, to interact with the fans. The video was shared on the Patriots’ official X account and instantly drew reactions from fans. “Listen, I knew we had fans in Germany, I didn’t know we had this many fans. Thank you for your support, go Pats, let’s raise a glass to everybody,” said Vrabel. The criticism continued to follow as the Patriots suffered a 35-10 defeat at the hands of the Lions on Sunday. Chris Long defends Mike Vrabel from beer drinking criticism Long played one season for the Patriots, but does not have much of an affiliation with Vrabel, who took over as head coach almost 8 years after Long left the team. However, he knew how things worked in the NFL, and spoke about how the decision to be at the event was not completely on the head coach. “The beer thing, I hate the look, okay? Like, make no mistake about it. When I saw it, I was like, ‘This is the dumbest s*** in the world. But it reeks of the NFL sending him to this thing on a Saturday, on the way to the hotel, and him coming in for 15 minutes, toasting with fans and drinking half a beer,” said Long on Green Light with Chris Long. “I saw this thing, and my problem is, if I see a bunch of people who don’t understand the context of something but are trying to make a big deal out of it, it drives me f****** nuts. It’s Germany; this is beer culture.” The Patriots’ defeat on Sunday could be more due to the injury to star quarterback Drake Maye, as opposed to Vrabel meeting the fans and having a little beer with them. However, with the Patriots currently holding a 5-5 record, all eyes will be on Vrabel, as he has already had a long offseason of controversy. And with this beer keg incident, it is clear that it is not going to be a great end to the season if the Patriots don’t win games. Brown message as Patriots trade disappointment grows Nick Wright says the Patriots made one of the worst NFL trades he’s seen in the last five years

item.title: Ajasa’s death painful loss to journalism, Vanguard — Atiku mourns
item.description: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has described the death of Vanguard Media Limited’s Online Editor, Olufemi Ajasa, as a painful loss to the journalism profession and the media organisation, extending his condolences to the management, staff and family of the deceased. Atiku, in a condolence message on his X handle on Tuesday, expressed sadness over Ajasa’s death at the age of 44, saying his passing was a reminder of how suddenly a life devoted to work, family and service could be cut short. He wrote, “Ajasa’s passing is a deep loss to @vanguardngrnews and to the journalism profession. Behind every story published and every deadline met is a commitment to keeping the public informed. “His colleagues have lost a valued teammate, the media community a respected professional, and his family a beloved son, husband, father and brother.” Atiku also extended his condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, the newspaper’s Editor, Eze Anaba, and everyone who knew and worked with the late journalist. “I extend my heartfelt condolences to the management and staff of Vanguard Media Limited, Editor Eze Anaba, and all who loved and worked with him,” the statement added. “May the memories they shared bring comfort in this difficult hour, and may God grant his family strength to bear this immeasurable loss. “May his soul rest in peace.” Ajasa died on Sunday at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital, LUTH, after a brief illness. He was aged 44, according to a statement by the management of Vanguard Media Limited. His death has continued to attract tributes from political figures, media practitioners and other Nigerians, who have mourned his passing and remembered his contributions to journalism. The post Ajasa’s death painful loss to journalism, Vanguard — Atiku mourns appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Statue planned for Johnny and Matthew Gaudreau at hometown rink
item.description: Johnny Gaudreau and his younger brother, Matthew , will have a statue outside their childhood ice rink in Sewell, New Jersey to honor their lives and hockey careers . More Blue Jackets news: How the Columbus Blue Jackets continue to keep Johnny Gaudreau's spirit alive The Gaudreau brothers were struck-and-killed by an SUV Aug. 29, 2024 while biking in Oldmans Township, New Jersey. Both starred at Boston College and Johnny became an NHL star who played his final two seasons with the Blue Jackets . According to a news release issued on Nov. 17, New Jersey-based artist Carl LeVotch will design the "Gaudreau Brothers Inspiration Sculpture," which is scheduled to be installed outside Hollydell Ice Arena in spring 2028. The Gaudreau brothers learned to skate and how to play hockey at Hollydell, where their father, Guy Gaudreau, served as director of the hockey programs. Guy and Jane Gaudreau, their mother, have endorsed the sculpture. “Hollydell is such an important part of John and Matty’s story," the Gaudreau parents said. "It’s where they first learned to love this game, and it will always hold a special place in our hearts as a family. That’s what makes it so meaningful to us that this piece of art will reside there." The sculpture will measure roughly 5 feet, 9 inches in height and be cast in bronze. It will sit on a base and weigh nearly 1,000 pounds. LeVotch's previous public bronze sculptures include monuments to boxing champions Jersey Joe Walcott in Camden, New Jersey, and Joey Giardello in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. He's working with Gaudreau Brothers Sculpture Project, a New Jersey-based non-profit to secure funding for the sculpture, and those wishing to donate can do so at gaudreaubrotherssculpture.org . LeVotch hopes to begin preliminary work on clay and wax models in December 2026 before casting a 17-inch model that will be used to create the final piece. "This sculpture looks beyond remembrance, as it is an invitation for every young athlete who encounters it to understand that character, compassion, and community are measures of greatness," LeVotch said in a statement. "The 'Gaudreau Brothers Inspiration Sculpture' is meant to serve as a lasting source of inspiration, encouraging every player, parent, coach, and visitor to carry those same values into their own lives.” Guy and Jane Gaudreau echoed those sentiments "As proud as we are of the players they became, we are even prouder of the people they were: kind, humble and devoted to their families and everyone around them. We hope every young player who walks through those doors sees it and is inspired to play the way John and Matty did: with heart and love for the game, and to live the way they did, with kindness on and off the ice. If it encourages even one kid to pick up a stick and follow their example, their legacy lives on." Dispatch Blue Jackets/Crew reporter Brian Hedger can be reached at bhedger@dispatch.com This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: Statue p

item.title: Dan Campbell won’t cut out celebrations despite Aidan Hutchinson injury
item.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Aidan Hutchinson of Detroit Lions celebrates sacking Drake Maye of New England Patriots before going down with an injury caused by celebrating during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) | Getty Images After Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL during a sack celebration , a huge debate ensued about whether Hutchinson was being reckless and selfish by putting himself in danger with the excessive celebration. A ton of Lions fans grew up in the era of Barry Sanders modestly handing off the football after touchdowns, so they’ve been accustomed to seeing players “act like they’ve been there before” and have a relative disdain for showboating. And given that this fanbase also witnessed a very similar injury to linebacker Stephen Tulloch in 2014, it’s not surprising that some are mad at Hutchinson. But don’t count Lions coach Dan Campbell among them. During his radio appearance on 97.1 The Ticket this week, Campbell was asked if he believed he needed to talk to the team about celebrations, given both Hutchinson’s injury and the amount of unsportsmanlike penalties the team has taken this year. He gave a pretty emphatic answer. “No, I don’t believe that. I think what happened speaks for itself. We’re not talking to eight-year-olds here,” Campbell said. Campbell then proceeded to tell a story about how he thinks he tore his bicep celebrating a play with just an emphatic arm-pump celebration, and that didn’t encourage him to tone down the emotions after a play. “So if you say, ‘Hey, don’t pump your arm next time, make sure you stay stoic,’ this game is built off of emotion,” Campbell said. “If you have to contain yourself after a play is made—I’m not talking about in the moment, in the game, because you’ve got to keep your head—then you’re really becoming something you’re not.” Ultimately, Campbell seemed to imply that this was just a freak accident. He’s seen Hutchinson do a ton of other incredibly athletic things that test the knee more than this celebration. He just got unlucky in the moment. “The number of moves that I’ve seen Hutch make and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one-leg—the lateral movements, lateral bounces,” Campbell said. “I’m just like—it was one of those things, man. I hate it. “But, no, I think we all understand what it is. Let’s be smart, but, no, I’m not going to say, ‘No one celebrates anymore.’” As for how the team will respond with Hutchinson now out for the year, Campbell said they’ll always be on the lookout for more talent to add to the roster—including claiming Tyrus West off waivers —but they are going to need several players to step up in his absence. But he’s confident. “We’re prepared to handle this storm. We are suited to handle this storm actually I think better tahn we were in ‘24. That’s the good news,” Campbel
item.content:encoded: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 15: Aidan Hutchinson of Detroit Lions celebrates sacking Drake Maye of New England Patriots before going down with an injury caused by celebrating during the NFL match between the New England Patriots and the Detroit Lions at the Allianz Arena on November 15, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) | Getty Images After Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL during a sack celebration , a huge debate ensued about whether Hutchinson was being reckless and selfish by putting himself in danger with the excessive celebration. A ton of Lions fans grew up in the era of Barry Sanders modestly handing off the football after touchdowns, so they’ve been accustomed to seeing players “act like they’ve been there before” and have a relative disdain for showboating. And given that this fanbase also witnessed a very similar injury to linebacker Stephen Tulloch in 2014, it’s not surprising that some are mad at Hutchinson. But don’t count Lions coach Dan Campbell among them. During his radio appearance on 97.1 The Ticket this week, Campbell was asked if he believed he needed to talk to the team about celebrations, given both Hutchinson’s injury and the amount of unsportsmanlike penalties the team has taken this year. He gave a pretty emphatic answer. “No, I don’t believe that. I think what happened speaks for itself. We’re not talking to eight-year-olds here,” Campbell said. Campbell then proceeded to tell a story about how he thinks he tore his bicep celebrating a play with just an emphatic arm-pump celebration, and that didn’t encourage him to tone down the emotions after a play. “So if you say, ‘Hey, don’t pump your arm next time, make sure you stay stoic,’ this game is built off of emotion,” Campbell said. “If you have to contain yourself after a play is made—I’m not talking about in the moment, in the game, because you’ve got to keep your head—then you’re really becoming something you’re not.” Ultimately, Campbell seemed to imply that this was just a freak accident. He’s seen Hutchinson do a ton of other incredibly athletic things that test the knee more than this celebration. He just got unlucky in the moment. “The number of moves that I’ve seen Hutch make and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one-leg—the lateral movements, lateral bounces,” Campbell said. “I’m just like—it was one of those things, man. I hate it. “But, no, I think we all understand what it is. Let’s be smart, but, no, I’m not going to say, ‘No one celebrates anymore.’” As for how the team will respond with Hutchinson now out for the year, Campbell said they’ll always be on the lookout for more talent to add to the roster—including claiming Tyrus West off waivers —but they are going to need several players to step up in his absence. But he’s confident. “We’re prepared to handle this storm. We are suited to handle this storm actually I think better tahn we were in ‘24. That’s the good news,” Campbell said. “Now, what has to happen, what can happen, and what will happen is that somebody’s got to pick up the slack. Somebody has to fill that void, and it’s not going to be one person, by the way. One person’s not going to fill the void of Aidan Hutchinson. “So it’s going to require (Alim McNeill) Mac to be at his very best. It’s going to require (DJ) Wonnum to be at his very best. It means Derrick Moore and Sky(ler) Gill-Howard are going to have to freakin’ step up and elevate their game. And Tyleik (Williams), we’re going to ask Tyleik to do more, too. So that’s really what you’re looking at, man. So, we’ve got resources here to handle this, but guys are going to have to fill that void. We’ve got to do it collectively. “The good news is we’re playing as one on defense. That really is our strength right now, we’re playing as one unit.”

item.title: Yankees make offer to coveted free agent reliever
item.description: The Yankees want free agent reliever Jonathan Loaisiga back for their bullpen rebuild after his first injury-free season in 2026 with the Diamondbacks. With lefty Tim Hill re-signed and a qualifying offer extended to closer David Bednar, the Yankees have offered a contract to Loaisiga, a source close to the Nicaraguan right-hander told NJ.com. The source requested anonymity to speak publicly about the situation. The Yankees’ offer is believed to be a one-year deal worth more than Loaisiga’s only other offer, a one-year, $5 million offer from the Diamondbacks. Loaisiga is seeking a three-year deal in the $18 million to $20 million range. The Dodgers, Mets and Phillies also have shown interest. The Yankees went into the offseason with six free-agent relievers and only one of their high-leverage arms under contract for next season: left-hander Brent Headrick. Bednar has until 4 p.m. ET Tuesday to accept a $23.15 million qualifying offer or hit the free agent market. If he passes on the qualifying offer, which is likely, the Yankees are expected to aggressively pursue a three-year deal at a lower annual pay day. Coming off another injury-plagued season in 2025, Loaisiga settled for a minor-league deal with the D’backs last January that included a $1.5 million salary in the majors. He proved to be a bargain, going 7-3 with a 2.42 ERA over a career-high 67 appearances. In addition to reducing homers allowed, Loaisiga averaged 97.9 mph on his sinker, while allowing 1.9 walks per nine innings and a barrel rate of 3.5%. Loaisiga, 32, started his major-league career pitching with the Yankees from 2018-25. He had a breakout season in 2021 when he was 9-4 with a 2.17 ERA in 57 outings, but he was on the injured list 10 times as a Yankee. Loaisiga wants to sign with someone before a probable work stoppage begins Dec. 1 at 11:59 p.m. “I know they want him to sign before the lockout,” the source said. “The Diamondbacks’ offer was weak and they were very clear telling him, ‘We want to lower our payroll.’” Loaisiga picked Arizona because he thought his career would benefit from pitching a full season in a warm-weather city and in the NL West, which is loaded with pitcher-friendly ballparks. “The Dodgers are an option that he likes because of the Los Angeles weather,” the source said. “They are interested, but have not made an offer. Same thing with the Phillies and Mets. No offer.” Loaisiga wants at least a two-year deal so he can get to 10 years’ service and qualify for a full pension. He’s currently at eight years and 22 days. “Two years is important to him because he wants to secure the 10 years,” the source said. As of 2026, a player with 10 years of service time qualifies for a full pension that pays $290,000 annually if the start date is at age 62. Retired players can get a reduced rate starting at age 45. item.title: Steve Kerr explains why Stephen Curry’s longevity is more impressive than that of Steve Nash, John Stockton
item.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Steve Kerr explains why Stephen Curry’s longevity is more impressive than that of Steve Nash, John Stockton appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry is out for at least two weeks due to an oblique injury he suffered against the Houston Rockets on November 12. It is the latest ailment for Curry, who has struggled to stay on the court in recent years. He was having a strong campaign before getting sidelined, leading the Warriors to an eight-game winning streak before losing to the Rockets. He was averaging 27.8 points, good for fifth-best in the league, 3.7 rebounds, and 3.9 assists. The Warriors are on a three-game skid, including the defeat to the Rockets, underscoring Curry’s value. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In a report from ESPN’s Anthony Slater, Warriors coach Steve Kerr said they have been extra cautious with the 38-year-old guard’s wear and tear . “The league has never been faster, more athletic, players sprinting around, the ground covered,” said Kerr. “Compared to Steve Nash or John Stockton , other guards of his ilk who were still playing at 38, 39, 40, the game’s a lot harder now.” While it was a sobering truth, Kerr also indirectly conveyed how impressive Curry’s longevity is. For comparison, at 38, Nash averaged 12.7 points, 2.8 rebounds, and 6.7 assists, while Stockton tallied 10.8 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 7.7 assists. They both retired at 41. Kerr is quite familiar with Nash and Stockton. He handled Nash when he was the general manager of the Phoenix Suns. They also reunited on the Warriors, with Nash serving as Kerr’s deputy. The four-time champion coach, meanwhile, had regular battles with Stockton when they were still playing. The Warriors want to have Curry on the floor , but they also need to ensure his long-term health. Handling the “dichotomy,” as Slater put it, of the 12-time All-Star is not easy. “Away from the fireworks show, Curry is in a constant race against time, obsessively evolving his body-maintenance plan in an effort to be available as often as possible—until the clock runs out,” wrote Slater. The clock is perpetually ticking, but Curry is not ready to walk away just yet. item.title: The All Blacks ‘let the country down’ in Wales defeat – here’s how they can respond against England
item.description: It seems the reports of the All Blacks ’ great rebirth were mildly exaggerated. On Monday afternoon, as he sought to make sense of first defeat to Wales in 73 years , the New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie was asked if that match actually mattered much in the context of the one to come against England this weekend. “Jeez, you’re not a Kiwi, are you?” Rennie said, half with a smile, half with a grimace. “We lost to Wales for the first time in 70-odd years; so, yeah, it matters all right. Sure, we’ll be highly motivated on the weekend, but we’re not going to brush last weekend’s result under the carpet. “We never use the word burden but we talk a lot about legacy and building on it. We took a step backwards last weekend. It’s important that we respond and try to add to the jersey.” Dave Rennie has spoken to his squad about the need to respond to a shock defeat to Wales (PA) The oft affable head coach had earlier suggested that he and his side had “let the country down” with their defeat; perhaps if, as Eddie Jones once suggested, the economy of New Zealand does really dip after each All Blacks defeat, that was not merely tough talking. As concerning as the result itself was the manner – yes, there were a number of changes, and all of Codie Taylor, Tupou Vaa’i, Cam Roigard, Damian McKenzie and Jordie Barrett will make a major difference on their return, but the fact that his side could not find a way through in the last 20 minutes in Cardiff might have had Rennie banging his head against a Welsh wall repeatedly in much the same way. That loss creates a certain sense of pressure on this trip to Twickenham. Between 2011 and 2020, New Zealand’s All Blacks were never beaten in back-to-back games. It has happened every calendar year bar one (2025) since – and that campaign culminated in the axing of Scott Robertson. That run was extended by three consecutive defeats in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series; if there can be no shame in pushing the current class of the international game in four Tests on foreign soil, the Springboks’ eventual 3-1 margin was resounding. New Zealand have endured a uniquely demanding year (Getty) That reflection, though, is maybe revealing when it comes to considering the context of where New Zealand find themselves. Even by the modern, unceasing standards of Test rugby, this has been a uniquely gruelling year. From their first encounter with France on 4 July until the end of November, the All Blacks will have played seven Nations Championship games, four Tests against the Springboks, four more Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour games and a couple of Bledisloe Cup clashes for good measure. Throw in the desperately sad news of the passing of long-time security chief Logan Cadwallader , which affected Rennie’s group significantly, and it is little wonder that performance levels slightly slipped against an inspired Wales. “This is the dream, playing for the All Blacks,” the hooker Asafo Aumua insisted, speaking of an extra edge to trai
item.content:encoded: It seems the reports of the All Blacks ’ great rebirth were mildly exaggerated. On Monday afternoon, as he sought to make sense of first defeat to Wales in 73 years , the New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie was asked if that match actually mattered much in the context of the one to come against England this weekend. “Jeez, you’re not a Kiwi, are you?” Rennie said, half with a smile, half with a grimace. “We lost to Wales for the first time in 70-odd years; so, yeah, it matters all right. Sure, we’ll be highly motivated on the weekend, but we’re not going to brush last weekend’s result under the carpet. “We never use the word burden but we talk a lot about legacy and building on it. We took a step backwards last weekend. It’s important that we respond and try to add to the jersey.” Dave Rennie has spoken to his squad about the need to respond to a shock defeat to Wales (PA) The oft affable head coach had earlier suggested that he and his side had “let the country down” with their defeat; perhaps if, as Eddie Jones once suggested, the economy of New Zealand does really dip after each All Blacks defeat, that was not merely tough talking. As concerning as the result itself was the manner – yes, there were a number of changes, and all of Codie Taylor, Tupou Vaa’i, Cam Roigard, Damian McKenzie and Jordie Barrett will make a major difference on their return, but the fact that his side could not find a way through in the last 20 minutes in Cardiff might have had Rennie banging his head against a Welsh wall repeatedly in much the same way. That loss creates a certain sense of pressure on this trip to Twickenham. Between 2011 and 2020, New Zealand’s All Blacks were never beaten in back-to-back games. It has happened every calendar year bar one (2025) since – and that campaign culminated in the axing of Scott Robertson. That run was extended by three consecutive defeats in the Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series; if there can be no shame in pushing the current class of the international game in four Tests on foreign soil, the Springboks’ eventual 3-1 margin was resounding. New Zealand have endured a uniquely demanding year (Getty) That reflection, though, is maybe revealing when it comes to considering the context of where New Zealand find themselves. Even by the modern, unceasing standards of Test rugby, this has been a uniquely gruelling year. From their first encounter with France on 4 July until the end of November, the All Blacks will have played seven Nations Championship games, four Tests against the Springboks, four more Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry tour games and a couple of Bledisloe Cup clashes for good measure. Throw in the desperately sad news of the passing of long-time security chief Logan Cadwallader , which affected Rennie’s group significantly, and it is little wonder that performance levels slightly slipped against an inspired Wales. “This is the dream, playing for the All Blacks,” the hooker Asafo Aumua insisted, speaking of an extra edge to training this week. “Sometimes you’ve got to reset each week, particularly after a result like that. You’ve got to pinch yourself – I’m still living my dream, even if we lost. “I feel like I have to lead from the front. Whenever I get the ball, put my head down and run as hard as I can. I was in all sorts after the game. It wasn’t up to our standard.” Asafo Aumua admits the All Blacks fell short of their standards (Reuters) There may be more to it, too. Rennie has made no secret of his desire to instil traditional values back into All Blacks rugby, in part by becoming less insular and recognising areas in need of improvement with influence from elsewhere; the attack coach Mike Blair, a Scot, is a great example . But the head coach has also been a hard taskmaster. He wants his side to run more and work harder than just about anyone else. “In the last two games, I didn’t quite hit a metric for the work rate,” the lock and former captain Scott Barrett revealingly remarked after his first two Tests back from injury. “I was doing extras at training, which is quite refreshing, actually. A little bit old school, but it’s clear where they want to go with the way they want to play the game.” After training on Tuesday, Rennie’s squad looked notably drained by a tough session in changeable conditions. The attrition rate has not been insignificant. Centre Quinn Tupaea and lock Jamie Hannah have joined the walking wounded this week, though there is increasing optimism that Will Jordan could be fit to start on the wing despite his hamstring tear . “He’s ahead of schedule on where we thought he would be,” Blair said. The squad has been operating without Ardie Savea , a vital force as much off the field as on it. Well-placed judges have wondered, too, if the famous depth has been denuded somewhat by the dissipating strength of Super Rugby . It is worth remembering, too, that Rennie came into his role after leading the Kobe Steelers to the Japan Rugby League One title in June. New Zealand are hopeful that Will Jordan will be fit to feature (Getty) All of this may feel an overreaction if, as they have so often before, New Zealand produce a response against England. Avoid an anomalous result against Wales and the All Blacks would have been back to No 1 in the world; they are indisputably contenders to win the World Cup next year. "We are all reflecting on what we could do better. You can't just blame it on the guys who take the field," Rennie said. "I should have done a better job last week. We picked a side that was a very good side and a side I was really confident that if we played to our potential would perform well. "It's disappointing and not good enough, but we've got to learn from it and bottle up the feeling post-game, because it hurts, and we have some pretty big footy coming up in the next few weeks and next year.”

item.title: Islanders Gameday News: Back home vs. the Jackets
item.description: Denying Son Of Sillinger. | Getty Images The Islanders return home from an all-too-rare successful Western trip to host the Columbus Blue Jackets, who are dragging the bottom of the division and conference. Taking five points on the trip helped inch Islanders back up toward the wild card spots, with three games in hand on the Panthers (27 points), who are five points ahead. The Blue Jackets are without head coach Rick Bowness, who has stepped away temporarily to tend to health issues. First Islanders Goal picks go here . Islanders News Previewing tonight: It’s yearbook night! (It’s funny, teams used to sell such things as pricey add-ons once they got you in the building with reasonable ticket prices; now they offer them as giveaways as enticements to get you in the building despite exorbitant ticket prices.) [ Isles ] With Logan Stanley “day to day,” Andrew Gross makes the case for Scott Mayfield. [ Newsday ] With Simon Holmstrom’s hat trick following a fourth-line demotion, Pete DeBoer says the winger has gotten his “work rate” back up as requested. [ Post ] Five takeaways from the California trip. [ Newsday ] Cal Ritchie is skating again (non contact). [ Isles ] Prospect Report: Vladimir Dravecky continues to pile up points, Luca Romano is on a run, too. [ Isles ] In the latest Islanders Anxiety, Mike and Dan relish a rare good week in California and the welcome sight of Mat Barzal back and feeling good. [ LHH ]

item.title: High school boys basketball: 2026 Class 4A team-by-team region capsules, predictions
item.description: The 2026-2027 high school boys basketball season gets underway this week with the official start of the season on Tuesday. To prepare fans for the upcoming season, the Deseret News has put together capsules for every team in 4A. Every coach was invited to participate and submit information. The region rankings are based on coaches preseason projections. There are 12 new head basketball coaches in 4A this year: Derek Newhof (Deer Creek), Sean Seastrand (Mountain View), Marcus Whimpey (Provo), Jace Tavita (Summit Academy), Jordan Hale (Wasatch), Cameron Cusworth (Cedar City), Charles Henderson (East), Mitch Smith (Juan Diego), Sam Hoopes (Judge Memorial), Drew Trost (Park City), Jake Christiansen (Sky View) and Dalten Stewart (Stansbury). Here are the 4A teams and players to watch this upcoming season. Region 8 1. Summit Academy Bears 2026-27 Schedule Head coach: Jace Tavita (1st year). 2025-26 record: 7-17 (fifth in Region 8 with a 1-7 record). 2026 RPI ranking: No. 23 in 4A. 2026 postseason: Lost to Timpanogos, 84-40, in the 4A first round. 2026 offense: 58.1 ppg (No. 18 in 4A) 2026 defense: 69.1 ppg (No. 26 in 4A) Returning starters: Two Returning contributors: Beckham Meredith, Sr. Dylan Kartchner, Sr. Key newcomers: Victor Lopez, Guard, So. Robby Dupuy, Guard, Fr. Coach comment: We’re excited for the season ahead. This group is hungry, competitive, and ready to prove what they can do. 2. Timpanogos Timberwolves 2026-27 Schedule Head coach: Golden Ingle (4th year). 2025-26 record: 13-14 (second in Region 8 with a 5-3 record). 2026 RPI ranking: No. 10 in 4A. 2026 postseason: Lost to Hurricane, 65-60, in the 4A semifinals. 2026 offense: 61.2 ppg (No. 10 in 4A) 2026 defense: 59 ppg (No. 19 in 4A) Returning starters: One Returning contributors: Miles Montague, Point Guard, Jr. Miles Riley, Forward, Sr. Key newcomers: Colt Vanchiere, Guard, Jr. Ethan Ranson, Guard, Jr. Mack McGuire, Forward, Jr. Coach comment: After a strong last season, we will look to build on it despite needing to replace six seniors, including Jaxen McCuistion, who led 4A in scoring. Filling that void will require a new approach and a commitment from every player on the roster to step into bigger roles. Led by a solid junior class and senior leadership, this team has worked hard this offseason developing in skill and chemistry. What we lack in size and experience, we plan to make up for in effort and toughness on every possession. A demanding preseason schedule will test us early, but expect this group to keep improving every day and be a tough, well-prepared opponent all season long. 3.
