item.content:encoded: The 2026-2027 high school boys basketball season gets underway this week with the official start of the season on Tuesday. To prepare fans for the upcoming season, the Deseret News has put together capsules for every team in 4A. Every coach was invited to participate and submit information. The region rankings are based on coaches preseason projections. There are 12 new head basketball coaches in 4A this year: Derek Newhof (Deer Creek), Sean Seastrand (Mountain View), Marcus Whimpey (Provo), Jace Tavita (Summit Academy), Jordan Hale (Wasatch), Cameron Cusworth (Cedar City), Charles Henderson (East), Mitch Smith (Juan Diego), Sam Hoopes (Judge Memorial), Drew Trost (Park City), Jake Christiansen (Sky View) and Dalten Stewart (Stansbury). Here are the 4A teams and players to watch this upcoming season. Region 8 1. Summit Academy Bears 2026-27 Schedule Head coach: Jace Tavita (1st year). 2025-26 record: 7-17 (fifth in Region 8 with a 1-7 record). 2026 RPI ranking: No. 23 in 4A. 2026 postseason: Lost to Timpanogos, 84-40, in the 4A first round. 2026 offense: 58.1 ppg (No. 18 in 4A) 2026 defense: 69.1 ppg (No. 26 in 4A) Returning starters: Two Returning contributors: Beckham Meredith, Sr. Dylan Kartchner, Sr. Key newcomers: Victor Lopez, Guard, So. Robby Dupuy, Guard, Fr. Coach comment: We’re excited for the season ahead. This group is hungry, competitive, and ready to prove what they can do. 2. Timpanogos Timberwolves 2026-27 Schedule Head coach: Golden Ingle (4th year). 2025-26 record: 13-14 (second in Region 8 with a 5-3 record). 2026 RPI ranking: No. 10 in 4A. 2026 postseason: Lost to Hurricane, 65-60, in the 4A semifinals. 2026 offense: 61.2 ppg (No. 10 in 4A) 2026 defense: 59 ppg (No. 19 in 4A) Returning starters: One Returning contributors: Miles Montague, Point Guard, Jr. Miles Riley, Forward, Sr. Key newcomers: Colt Vanchiere, Guard, Jr. Ethan Ranson, Guard, Jr. Mack McGuire, Forward, Jr. Coach comment: After a strong last season, we will look to build on it despite needing to replace six seniors, including Jaxen McCuistion, who led 4A in scoring. Filling that void will require a new approach and a commitment from every player on the roster to step into bigger roles. Led by a solid junior class and senior leadership, this team has worked hard this offseason developing in skill and chemistry. What we lack in size and experience, we plan to make up for in effort and toughness on every possession. A demanding preseason schedule will test us early, but expect this group to keep improving every day and be a tough, well-prepared opponent all season long. 3. Provo Bulldogs 2026-27 Schedule Head coach: Marcus Whimpey (1st year). 2025-26 record: 23-4 (first in Region 8 with a 7-1 record). 2026 RPI ranking: No. 1 in 4A. 2026 postseason: Beat Hurricane, 62-42, in the 4A championship. 2026 offense: 66.1 ppg (No. 1 in 4A) 2026 defense: 53.1 ppg (No. 5 in 4A) Returning starters: None Returning contributors: Malik Allen, Point Guard, Jr. Emanuel Hiraldo, Forward, Jr. Cameron Rust, Forward, Jr. Key newcomers: Chauncey Ako, Forward, Sr. T-Ray Brenchley, Guard, Jr. Boz Richards, Guard, Jr. Kaleb Tollestrup, Forward, So. Boden Bassett, Guard, So. Noah Castagnetto, Forward, Fr. Tre Akina, Guard, Fr. Coach comment: We lose 8 seniors from our state championship team and a lot of leadership from that group. We love what they did and what they mean to Provo Basketball. They set the example and expectations moving forward. We have a really young team (only 2 seniors), with a lot of talent up and coming! We have a lot of kids that sit in the 6’2 to 6’4 range that will give us versatility on how we play on both sides of the floor! The potential is there; the key is how fast these young guys can gel, get used to the varsity level, and play high-level defense! Excited for these new fellas to show us what they’ve got and represent the great tradition of Provo Basketball. 4. Wasatch Wasps 2026-27 Schedule Head coach: Jordan Hale (1st year). 2025-26 record: 19-6 (fourth in Region 7 with a 4-4 record). 2026 RPI ranking: No. 4 in 5A. 2026 postseason: Lost to Pleasant Grove, 65-58, in the 5A quarterfinals. 2026 offense: 68.8 ppg (No. 4 in 5A) 2026 defense: 59.6 ppg (No. 18 in 5A) Returning starters: One Returning contributors: Caleb Balch, Guard, Sr. Cole Moore, Guard/Forward, Sr. Key newcomers: Gage Widdison, Guard/Forward, Sr. Johann Hoffman, Forward/Center, Jr. Sam Hinckley, Guard/Forward, Jr. Peyton Morris, Guard, Jr. Coach comment: This year is going to be really great for us. We have a lot of really talented guys who haven’t gotten as much opportunity because of last year’s outstanding senior class. This year will be their opportunity to showcase their talents and prove they can hang in this year’s tough 4A. 5. There’s a lot of excitement about what our group can do together. 6. Uintah Utes 2026-27 Schedule Head coach: Mitch Argyle (2nd year). 2025-26 record: 9-15 (fourth in Region 8 with a 3-5 record). 2026 RPI ranking: No. 19 in 4A. 2026 postseason: Lost to Murray, 52-46, in the 4A first round. 2026 offense: 53.2 ppg (No. 24 in 4A) 2026 defense: 56 ppg (No. 9 in 4A) Returning starters: Three Returning contributors: CJ Briggs, Guard, Sr. Adam Wallis, Post, Sr. Landon Woods, Post, Sr. Sean Eaton, Wing, Sr. Ryker Ewing, Guard, Sr. Brody Murray, Wing, Sr. Key newcomers: Karson Baum, Guard, Sr. Grady Marshall, Wing, Jr. Ashton Argyle, Post, Jr. Coach comment: We are excited about the offseason work our program put in. item.title: College football AP Top 25 schedule for Week 12 is worst in nearly 20 years
item.description: We have been spoiled with some great college football games each and every week. And with just two regular season weeks left, games should mean more and more. But that might not be the case in Week 12. Of course, the games matter, especially for those teams that are on the bubble of making the College Football Playoff , but in terms of ranked games? There won’t be any. According to On3’s Brett McMurphy , it’s the first time since 2009 that there won’t be any AP Top 25 -ranked matchups in the month of November. Just this past week, we saw five ranked-on-ranked games throughout Saturday. In Week 10, there were even more, with seven games that featured ranked-on-ranked matchups. That’s been the staple this season, with upsets affecting the rankings each and every week. MORE : Predicting College Football Playoff Rankings Entering Week 12 of 2026 Season Are there any games worth watching? Nov 14, 2026; Columbus, Ohio, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Luke Fahey (13) drops to throw during the first quarter against the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) If you’re a college football lover, you’re going to watch the games either way. But if you’re looking for certain games to watch because of implications, we have you covered. It would be odd to see Ohio State miss the playoff, but that’s looking more likely. However, if the Buckeyes have any shot of making it, they need to take care of business this week against Nebraska and next week against Michigan. Style points are going to matter, and this weekend Ohio State is in Lincoln to play the Huskers. That game will start at Noon ET on Fox, and it’s worth seeing if Ohio State can take a step forward with freshman Luke Fahey behind center. There are implications in the Big 12 and Texas Tech is at the heart of it. The Red Raiders control their own destiny to play Utah, and Texas Tech hits the road against a stingy Baylor defense. That’s at 3:30 p.m. ET on Fox. And while Notre Dame isn’t in a conference, this game was circled several weeks ago. Notre Dame hosts SMU and it’s the Irish’s last game; it feels like they could lose on the schedule. After SMU was blasted last weekend against Wake Forest, it doesn’t feel like a big game, but the Mustangs can put up a lot of points. That game will kick off at 7:30 p.m. ET on NBC. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: High school football: 5A state championship preview, powerhouses Orem-West set for Rice-Eccles Stadium rematch
item.description: Orem plays Woods Cross in a 5A semifinal football game at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. Orem won 56-10, with the game ending at the end of the third quarter for the mercy rule. | Kristin Murphy, Deseret News 5A Championship No. 2 Orem (10-2) vs. No. 1 West (13-0) 5A championship Friday, Nov. 20, 11 a.m., at the University of Utah Parry’s Power Guide: Orem by 9 All-time series: Tied 2-2 (since 1961) Last meeting: Orem won 34-7 at the University of Utah (Nov. 13, 2025, 5A semifinals) How the Tigers got here Orem started the season with a new head coach and a state title to defend. Andy Stokes came over after three years as Crimson Cliffs’ offensive coordinator, and the Tigers lost two of their first three games. Both losses came against top out-of-state and 6A opponents: 21-14 at Skyridge, a 6A semifinalist, and 32-26 to Mater Dei (Calif.). Orem hasn’t lost since. The Tigers have won nine straight, won Region 7 outright at 6-0 and haven’t played a close game in the playoffs. They beat Timpview 55-7 and Pleasant Grove 35-16, then ended Woods Cross’ run as a No. 14 seed with a 56-10 semifinal win stopped by the mercy rule after three quarters. Tanner Lewis threw only one incompletion in that game, and six different players scored touchdowns. “I think we’re playing our best football right now, but I think we could be better,” Stokes said afterward. Orem plays Woods Cross in a 5A semifinal football game at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. | Kristin Murphy, Deseret News What the Tigers need to do to win Orem has to do to West what it did a year ago, which is win at the line of scrimmage. item.content:encoded: Orem plays Woods Cross in a 5A semifinal football game at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. Orem won 56-10, with the game ending at the end of the third quarter for the mercy rule. | Kristin Murphy, Deseret News 5A Championship No. 2 Orem (10-2) vs. No. 1 West (13-0) 5A championship Friday, Nov. 20, 11 a.m., at the University of Utah Parry’s Power Guide: Orem by 9 All-time series: Tied 2-2 (since 1961) Last meeting: Orem won 34-7 at the University of Utah (Nov. 13, 2025, 5A semifinals) How the Tigers got here Orem started the season with a new head coach and a state title to defend. Andy Stokes came over after three years as Crimson Cliffs’ offensive coordinator, and the Tigers lost two of their first three games. Both losses came against top out-of-state and 6A opponents: 21-14 at Skyridge, a 6A semifinalist, and 32-26 to Mater Dei (Calif.). Orem hasn’t lost since. The Tigers have won nine straight, won Region 7 outright at 6-0 and haven’t played a close game in the playoffs. They beat Timpview 55-7 and Pleasant Grove 35-16, then ended Woods Cross’ run as a No. 14 seed with a 56-10 semifinal win stopped by the mercy rule after three quarters. Tanner Lewis threw only one incompletion in that game, and six different players scored touchdowns. “I think we’re playing our best football right now, but I think we could be better,” Stokes said afterward. Orem plays Woods Cross in a 5A semifinal football game at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026. | Kristin Murphy, Deseret News What the Tigers need to do to win Orem has to do to West what it did a year ago, which is win at the line of scrimmage. In last year’s semifinal on this same field, the Tigers built an early three-touchdown lead and won 34-7. West quarterback Kamden Lopati separated his shoulder in the second quarter of that game. The Tigers have the players to do it again. Their defense allows 13.3 points per game, second in 5A behind West. Major Stokes and Jag Ioane have 10 sacks each, and Krew Jones, a four-star Oklahoma commit, has six. Orem has six defensive touchdowns. JaVoni Halalilo has scored twice and Kaio Akana leads the team with four interceptions. West has scored at least 20 points in every game this season, but no defense it has faced has a pass rush like Orem’s. On offense, Orem is efficient and hard to slow down. Lewis has completed 65.1% of his passes for 1,950 yards and 28 touchdowns and has thrown two interceptions all season. Brooks Ross averages 19.6 yards per catch and has 13 touchdown catches. Po Faumui has 49 catches and 12 total touchdowns, two of them on defense. Beckham Curtis has run for 1,469 yards and 16 total touchdowns at 8.5 yards per carry. Lewis credited the team’s depth after the semifinal. “We’ve got deep, deep personnel,” he said. The challenge is that West’s defense allows 5.5 points per game. Orem can’t afford mistakes, and it needs Curtis to keep the offense on schedule so Lewis isn’t throwing into a secondary that has returned interceptions for touchdowns. A win would give Orem back-to-back titles, its sixth championship since 2017 and the ninth in program history. How the Panthers got here West has been the most dominant team in Utah all season. The Panthers are 13-0 and have outscored opponents 668-71. They shut out five straight teams before last week’s 29-12 semifinal win over Bountiful. Their only close games came against out-of-state opponents in August. The semifinal was also a chance at redemption. A year ago West entered the semifinals as the No. 1 seed and fell behind Orem by three touchdowns early. This time the Panthers opened with two long scoring drives, led 21-0 at halftime and held Bountiful to 137 total yards. Lopati hurt his finger four plays into the game, and freshman Sam Arona led the opening touchdown drive while he was treated. Lopati returned and finished with three touchdowns. The win sends West to its first title game since 1992, which was also the last time the Rose Park school won a state title. Senior Samanu Tua’one explained what that means to his neighborhood. “I grew up in Rose Park. We’ve always been bad, but I’m excited to play next week, especially with all the kids,” he said. West Panthers quarterback Sam Arona (9), left, hands the ball off to running back Naeata Hamilton (22) during the first half of a 5A semifinal high school football game against the Bountiful Redhawks, Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City. | Erin Hooley, Deseret News What the Panthers need to do to win West needs to win the line of scrimmage, where it lost to Orem a year ago. The Panthers’ defense might be the best in the state. It has 49 sacks. Takeshi Savery has 13, Dieter Lotulelei has 11 and Samauel Chein-Tauvao has seven. Bountiful finished the semifinal with minus-19 rushing yards. Tua’one has four interceptions and three touchdowns. Lester Falatea has six interceptions, three defensive touchdowns and seven return touchdowns, which makes him the player most likely to turn the game with one play. Lopati is healthy and running an offense that averages 51.4 points per game. He has completed 70% of his passes for 3,182 yards and 31 touchdowns, and he has run for 832 yards and 12 more, for 43 total touchdowns. Mani Tu’uao averages 23.7 yards per catch and Monson Vaenuku averages 27.8. Naeata Hamilton has run for 1,105 yards and 16 total touchdowns. The biggest concern is discipline. West set a state playoff record with 220 penalty yards against Bountiful, and every first down Bountiful earned in the first three quarters came on a West penalty. Orem’s offense won’t need that much help. “We can’t leave that up for chance,” coach Olosaa Solovi said. “We got to be better there, and we got to be smarter.” The two teams have no common opponents. Both have played strong out-of-state teams. Orem lost to Mater Dei, while West beat Archbishop Riordan 21-13. If West avoids penalties and keeps Lopati upright, it has the talent to win the program’s first title in 34 years. item.title: Rooney says he considered taking his own life at Man Utd
item.description: Rooney scored 53 goals in 120 appearances for England [Getty Images] Warning: This article contains references to suicide Wayne Rooney says he was "contemplating suicide" during his playing days at Manchester United and was "speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up". The former England captain joined United from Everton in 2004 and went on to become the club's record goalscorer, with 253 goals in 559 appearances. But Rooney, speaking with Gabby Logan on the Life at the Midpoint podcast , detailed his struggles off the pitch when eldest son Kai, who is now 17, was a baby. "When I was drinking, I would lock myself in my house for two days and just drink," said Rooney, when asked about the lowest point in his life. "This is probably in my best part of my career playing wise." The 41-year-old went on to explain how he "struggled to deal with it all" and, after opening up to his wife Coleen and his mother, knew he "needed help to get through it". "I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with," he added. "I didn't want Kai seeing me like that, so that's why I'd hide away as well. "I got to a place where you're contemplating suicide. I just didn't want to be around anyone. I didn't want to see people in the streets. I didn't want to go into shops. "I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else, [I] really struggled with it." Rooney, who scored 53 goals in 120 England appearances, was recently named pundit of the year at the Broadcast Sport Awards and is currently appearing on reality TV show I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here. He helped United win five Premier League titles, the Champions League, Europa League, FA Cup and three EFL Cups before leaving them to return to the Toffees in 2017. But the former forward said he learned to mask his feelings during his lowest moments. "You don't want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it," Rooney added. "Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man, if you like, for doing that. "I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I've just had a young son, I've just been married. "It should be the happiest point in my life and it wasn't. "It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking. "Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it." If you have been affected by issues raised in this article, there is information and support available on BBC Action Line. item.title: ₦70,000 Transport Controversy: FG Constitutes Committee To Review New Minimum Wages For Workers
item.description: The Federal Government has approved the constitution of a new committee to comprehensively examine and address the issues raised by the Trade Union Congress (TUC) regarding a new minimum wage for Nigerian workers. The development was revealed by the TUC’s Secretary-General, Comrade General N.A. Toro, in a statement on Tuesday, following a meeting with the Federal Government in response to a letter dated 8th October, 2026, titled “Request for an Urgent Meeting to Address Critical National Economic, Security and Labour Challenges,” submitted by the Union. TUC President, Alex Osifo, in handshake with Ayo Fayose during the meeting While the meeting was chaired by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, the TUC delegation was led by the President, Comrade Engr. Festus Osifo, and comprised Comrade General N.A. Toro, Secretary-General; Comrade Shehu Mohammed, Deputy President; Comrade Akintola Benjamin, Trustee; and Comrade Kamal Ibrahim, Auditor II. Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, during the meeting Also in attendance were the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation and the Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Ibrahim Kana. While providing further explanation, TUC noted that it had insisted on a salary increment rather than a mere one-off N70,000 six-month transportation package. “In the course of the deliberations, the TUC made its position unequivocally clear on the proposed ₦70,000 transport intervention for a period of six months, which it rejected, preferring instead a salary increase pending the commencement and conclusion of discussions on a new National Minimum Wage. “This position, alongside the other demands and concerns raised by Congress, will form part of the issues to be thoroughly interrogated by the High-Powered Committee”, the statement read in part. According to the statement, the government has already attended to some of the demands raised by the TUC. “The Committee will therefore undertake a comprehensive review and reconciliation of the issues, establish the extent of actions already taken by the Government, identify outstanding matters and make appropriate findings and recommendations”, the statement said in part. The composition of the High-Powered Committee includes three representatives from the TUC, led by the Secretary-General, Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (OSGF), Permanent Secretary, Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation (OHCSF), National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, and the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment. The High-Powered Committee is expected to commence work immediately and submit its report to the Secretary to the Government of the Federation within two weeks. The post ₦70,000 Transport Controversy: FG Constitutes Committee To Review New Minimum Wages For Workers appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: ‘Nigeria is finished’ narrative costing economy investments, jobs — FG
item.description: By John Alechenu, Abuja The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said Nigeria is paying a heavy economic price for negative narratives, misinformation and damaging perceptions about the country. Negative stories, he said, are not merely public relations problems. They discourage investors, constrain businesses, and drive away skilled talent. Oyedele spoke at the ongoing 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) in Abuja on Tuesday. He identified public trust as a critical factor in attracting investment, sustaining businesses and securing citizens’ support for government policies. According to him, trust is the currency that underpins economic activities and determines whether citizens cooperate with government, investors commit capital and businesses expand. Oyedele said, “Trust is the one currency that sits beneath all the other currencies. When trust is strong, citizens cooperate, capital flows, businesses invest, and reforms get a fair hearing. When trust is weak, even sound policies meet suspicion, and every explanation sounds like an excuse.” The minister said the economic consequences of negative narratives are often overlooked. The country could lose investments and valuable human capital when its public image was dominated by stories of failure and hopelessness. He cited damaging perceptions expressed in phrases such as “Nigeria is finished”, “Nigeria is a scam”, and “Nigeria happened to me”, warning that such narratives could influence investment decisions and undermine confidence in the country’s economic prospects. Oyedele further explained that the cost went beyond reputational damage. Investors demand higher returns to compensate for perceived risks, businesses postpone expansion plans, and talented Nigerians seek opportunities elsewhere. He, however, acknowledged that citizens have the right to expose government failures, demand accountability and draw attention to the difficulties they faced. Responsible communication, he insisted, must not be confused with suppressing criticism. The country’s story must reflect both its challenges and progress, he added. Government and businesses could not rely on publicity to conceal poor performance or substitute communication for service delivery. “We cannot communicate our way out of conflicts,” he said. Oyedele stressed that public communication must be backed by measurable results. Citizens judged government not by announcements or budgetary provisions but by what they experienced. The minister noted that the disconnect between government claims and citizens’ everyday experiences had contributed to distrust, making it difficult for even well-intentioned policies to gain public acceptance. He used the public’s response to declining inflation figures to illustrate the challenge. item.content:encoded: By John Alechenu, Abuja The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said Nigeria is paying a heavy economic price for negative narratives, misinformation and damaging perceptions about the country. Negative stories, he said, are not merely public relations problems. They discourage investors, constrain businesses, and drive away skilled talent. Oyedele spoke at the ongoing 2026 World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) in Abuja on Tuesday. He identified public trust as a critical factor in attracting investment, sustaining businesses and securing citizens’ support for government policies. According to him, trust is the currency that underpins economic activities and determines whether citizens cooperate with government, investors commit capital and businesses expand. Oyedele said, “Trust is the one currency that sits beneath all the other currencies. When trust is strong, citizens cooperate, capital flows, businesses invest, and reforms get a fair hearing. When trust is weak, even sound policies meet suspicion, and every explanation sounds like an excuse.” The minister said the economic consequences of negative narratives are often overlooked. The country could lose investments and valuable human capital when its public image was dominated by stories of failure and hopelessness. He cited damaging perceptions expressed in phrases such as “Nigeria is finished”, “Nigeria is a scam”, and “Nigeria happened to me”, warning that such narratives could influence investment decisions and undermine confidence in the country’s economic prospects. Oyedele further explained that the cost went beyond reputational damage. Investors demand higher returns to compensate for perceived risks, businesses postpone expansion plans, and talented Nigerians seek opportunities elsewhere. He, however, acknowledged that citizens have the right to expose government failures, demand accountability and draw attention to the difficulties they faced. Responsible communication, he insisted, must not be confused with suppressing criticism. The country’s story must reflect both its challenges and progress, he added. Government and businesses could not rely on publicity to conceal poor performance or substitute communication for service delivery. “We cannot communicate our way out of conflicts,” he said. Oyedele stressed that public communication must be backed by measurable results. Citizens judged government not by announcements or budgetary provisions but by what they experienced. The minister noted that the disconnect between government claims and citizens’ everyday experiences had contributed to distrust, making it difficult for even well-intentioned policies to gain public acceptance. He used the public’s response to declining inflation figures to illustrate the challenge. Although the October 2026 inflation rate was reported at 14.06 per cent, the lowest in six years, many Nigerians remain unconvinced because prices of essential commodities such as bread and milk were still high. Oyedele equally explained that a decline in inflation did not mean prices were falling but that the rate at which prices increased was slowing down. Failure to explain that distinction, he said, could deepen frustration and create expectations that further influence market behaviour. In the controversy surrounding the government’s tax reforms, Oyedele said misinformation had distorted the intention and benefits of the measures, including provisions designed to protect small businesses and exempt low-income earners. Some of the people the reforms were intended to benefit had opposed them because of misleading information, he said, underscoring the need for clear and sustained public engagement. “Facts do not defend themselves,” he said, adding that “in a contest between a careful explanation and a frightening headline, the headline wins.” The minister also expressed concern about social media platforms, where sensational and divisive content often attracts more attention than factual corrections. “Outrage pays, correction does not,” he said. He warned that the growing use of artificial intelligence had made the spread of misinformation more dangerous, as convincing images, voices and documents could now be fabricated and circulated rapidly. Oyedele urged public relations and communication professionals to become involved in policy formulation from the beginning rather than being brought in only when government or businesses faced communication crises. He challenged media organisations, influencers and other information gatekeepers to take greater responsibility for the content they circulate. “Verify before you amplify. Correct as loudly as you reported when you make mistakes. Hold good news and bad news to the same standard of proof,” he urged. He also called on government institutions and businesses to make policy and economic information accessible, respond to public complaints and measure the effectiveness of their communication by whether people understood the message and could see the results. Oyedele maintained that the credibility of any national or corporate narrative ultimately depended on the lived experiences of the people, not the volume of publicity deployed to promote it. “Experiencing is knowing,” he said. item.title: Northwestern got bullied by Columbia. Now what?
item.description: 57 years. That’s the last time Columbia beat a Big Ten team. But on Monday night in Welsh-Ryan Arena, that streak finally ended in devastating fashion for the Wildcats. A 75-53 loss ended that decades-long streak and set off early-season alarm bells for the Wildcats. The Lions led by as many as 26 late in the game, and it was the second straight loss by more than 20 points, dropping the team to 3-2 early in the season. “It’s hard to find any silver linings, really,” head coach Chris Collins said postgame. “Just a little bit shocked, a little bit stunned by how we played tonight. But it’s kind of who we are right now.” With little margin for error, NU couldn’t play with force against a team it were projected to handle with ease. The numbers show the clearest picture. Northwestern had taken just six free throws all game, while Columbia took four times as many. The Lions also grabbed 38.7% of their own misses, yielding a 15-8 edge in second-chance points. Seven Columbia players finished with at least three rebounds, including guard Hampton Sanders, who grabbed six despite being listed at 6-foot, though Collins guessed he’s “maybe 5-foot-9”. “It was not just their bigger bodies,” Collins said. “It was a collection of their mindset of playing with physicality, and we just don’t have it right now. We’re getting beat to balls, we’re getting pushed under the rim, it’s guards, it’s bigs, it’s everybody .” Losing size hasn’t helped that cause. Collins said the team will be without redshirt junior Ryan Soulis for an indefinite period due to a foot injury that requires surgery, alongside redshirt junior Luke McEldon, taking a leave of absence. Without them, Northwestern has played 6-foot-9 junior Okku Federiko at center, who’s only played power forward at the collegiate level. Collins didn’t make excuses, saying the absences didn’t explain the rebounding issue. “It’s not an excuse with having guys out,” he said. “It’s a mindset.” Despite offensive struggles to start, Northwestern still the lead 13 minutes into Monday’s contest. Angelo Ciaravino sank a jumper with 7:20 left in the first half that put the ‘Cats up 17-11. But while Northwestern’s struggles lingered in the first half, Columbia started to surge. The Lions closed the half on a 17-2 run and led 28-19 after 20 minutes. The Wildcats shot 7-of-27 from the field and 1-for-11 from deep. Collins said the team got a lot of open looks but missed many, which affected the team’s energy. “I thought our heads got down a little bit,” he said. item.content:encoded: 57 years. That’s the last time Columbia beat a Big Ten team. But on Monday night in Welsh-Ryan Arena, that streak finally ended in devastating fashion for the Wildcats. A 75-53 loss ended that decades-long streak and set off early-season alarm bells for the Wildcats. The Lions led by as many as 26 late in the game, and it was the second straight loss by more than 20 points, dropping the team to 3-2 early in the season. “It’s hard to find any silver linings, really,” head coach Chris Collins said postgame. “Just a little bit shocked, a little bit stunned by how we played tonight. But it’s kind of who we are right now.” With little margin for error, NU couldn’t play with force against a team it were projected to handle with ease. The numbers show the clearest picture. Northwestern had taken just six free throws all game, while Columbia took four times as many. The Lions also grabbed 38.7% of their own misses, yielding a 15-8 edge in second-chance points. Seven Columbia players finished with at least three rebounds, including guard Hampton Sanders, who grabbed six despite being listed at 6-foot, though Collins guessed he’s “maybe 5-foot-9”. “It was not just their bigger bodies,” Collins said. “It was a collection of their mindset of playing with physicality, and we just don’t have it right now. We’re getting beat to balls, we’re getting pushed under the rim, it’s guards, it’s bigs, it’s everybody .” Losing size hasn’t helped that cause. Collins said the team will be without redshirt junior Ryan Soulis for an indefinite period due to a foot injury that requires surgery, alongside redshirt junior Luke McEldon, taking a leave of absence. Without them, Northwestern has played 6-foot-9 junior Okku Federiko at center, who’s only played power forward at the collegiate level. Collins didn’t make excuses, saying the absences didn’t explain the rebounding issue. “It’s not an excuse with having guys out,” he said. “It’s a mindset.” Despite offensive struggles to start, Northwestern still the lead 13 minutes into Monday’s contest. Angelo Ciaravino sank a jumper with 7:20 left in the first half that put the ‘Cats up 17-11. But while Northwestern’s struggles lingered in the first half, Columbia started to surge. The Lions closed the half on a 17-2 run and led 28-19 after 20 minutes. The Wildcats shot 7-of-27 from the field and 1-for-11 from deep. Collins said the team got a lot of open looks but missed many, which affected the team’s energy. “I thought our heads got down a little bit,” he said. After halftime, Northwestern tightened the gap to five points, but Columbia answered each time. Gerard O’Keefe scored 14 of his game-high 20 points in the half, shooting 5-for-6 inside the arc. Collins said the defense broke down during that span, ignored its gameplan and allowed the Lions to find easy layups. Columbia also had an effective plan for guarding Jake West, who had scored 20+ points in every game up until Monday, by trapping him on ball screens and forcing another Wildcat to beat them. West finished with just nine points on 4-of-12 shooting, along with four assists and three turnovers. He was blunt about the source of the team’s struggles after the game. “This loss is on me,” West said. “I got to be better. I got to be more mature as a player.” Collins took the blame himself. “I got to do a better job. My staff has to do a better job of trying to be competitive with what we have right now.” Northwestern’s schedule gives them little time to make adjustments. The Wildcats head to Charleston, South Carolina, for their first away game of the year against their first Power Five team, Virginia Tech, on Wednesday and then again that Friday against Dayton. Asked whether they’ll be able to recover from the disappointing start, Collins sounded more exasperated than he did assured. “I mean, if so, we should just cancel the games,” he said. “We have to get better. We got to play better…I’m not ready to cancel the season yet.” Whether Northwestern can find that edge will be answered in Charleston, and it will say a lot more about where the season is headed from here.

item.title: “I’m Being More American”: Brittney Griner Reveals Why the Un-American Label Still Hurts
item.description: Aug 7, 2026; Uncasville, Connecticut, USA; Connecticut Sun center Brittney Griner (42) reacts after a non call against the Phoenix Mercury in the second half at Mohegan Sun Arena. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images Few athletes carry a label as heavy as the one Brittney Griner says follows her home. Years after a Russian penal colony and a high-profile prisoner swap, one word still stings more than any other. That word is un-American. Griner addressed it in a conversation with Cam Newton on his YouTube channel, and she did not hold back. Griner says the criticism ties back to her detainment in Russia and to the man the United States sent in exchange. She was freed in December 2022 in a swap for Viktor Bout, a Russian arms dealer serving 25 years in a U.S. prison. Public opinion split sharply, and critics argued the deal sent the wrong message to American adversaries. Griner says people talk as if she was the one dictating the terms. The swap came on the initiative of then-President Joe Biden, and she had no say in who stood on the other side. She also says she wanted to fight for her country, and still got the label. “ People say I’m un-American. And it kind of goes with my detainment and coming back and who I was traded for, as if I was the person dictating everything back there,” Griner said to Cam Newton on his YouTube channel. “ Like I was calling and saying like, ‘Hey, trade me for this person or do this.’ For some reason I got labeled un-American when I mean, I wanted to fight for this country. ” Griner is not rejecting patriotism. She is redefining it on her own terms, with the Constitution as her backup. She also made clear this is not an attack on police. Griner called her father her biggest hero and said she supports officers. But she will not pretend every officer is doing a great job. Her upbringing, she says, backs up the claim. Veterans Day was the biggest holiday in her childhood home because her family supports the troops. Griner planned to enlist, then move into law enforcement, until high school. She is a WNBA champion with three Olympic gold medals and two World Cup golds for Team USA. Then came February 2022. Russian officials detained Griner at a Moscow-area airport after finding vape cartridges with hashish oil in her luggage. She had flown in to play during the WNBA offseason, and she would spend about 10 months in custody. She received a nine-year sentence in August 2022 and was later moved to the IK-2 penal colony in Mordovia. She was forced to make uniforms for Russian soldiers there. Inside the colony, her identity was already set. Griner has described how fellow inmates saw her. “ Everyone knew ‘the American.’ That was my title ,” she has said. item.content:encoded: Aug 7, 2026; Uncasville, Connecticut, USA; Connecticut Sun center Brittney Griner (42) reacts after a non call against the Phoenix Mercury in the second half at Mohegan Sun Arena. Mandatory Credit: David Butler II-Imagn Images Few athletes carry a label as heavy as the one Brittney Griner says follows her home. Years after a Russian penal colony and a high-profile prisoner swap, one word still stings more than any other. That word is un-American. Griner addressed it in a conversation with Cam Newton on his YouTube channel, and she did not hold back. Griner says the criticism ties back to her detainment in Russia and to the man the United States sent in exchange. She was freed in December 2022 in a swap for Viktor Bout, a Russian arms dealer serving 25 years in a U.S. prison. Public opinion split sharply, and critics argued the deal sent the wrong message to American adversaries. Griner says people talk as if she was the one dictating the terms. The swap came on the initiative of then-President Joe Biden, and she had no say in who stood on the other side. And it kind of goes with my detainment and coming back and who I was traded for, as if I was the person dictating everything back there,” Griner said to Cam Newton on his YouTube channel. “ Like I was calling and saying like, ‘Hey, trade me for this person or do this.’ For some reason I got labeled un-American when I mean, I wanted to fight for this country. ” Griner is not rejecting patriotism. She is redefining it on her own terms, with the Constitution as her backup. She also made clear this is not an attack on police. Griner called her father her biggest hero and said she supports officers. But she will not pretend every officer is doing a great job. Her upbringing, she says, backs up the claim. Veterans Day was the biggest holiday in her childhood home because her family supports the troops. Griner planned to enlist, then move into law enforcement, until high school. She is a WNBA champion with three Olympic gold medals and two World Cup golds for Team USA. Then came February 2022. Russian officials detained Griner at a Moscow-area airport after finding vape cartridges with hashish oil in her luggage. She had flown in to play during the WNBA offseason, and she would spend about 10 months in custody. She received a nine-year sentence in August 2022 and was later moved to the IK-2 penal colony in Mordovia. She was forced to make uniforms for Russian soldiers there. Inside the colony, her identity was already set. Griner has described how fellow inmates saw her. “ Everyone knew ‘the American.’ That was my title ,” she has said. In a Russian prison, she was the American. Back home, she says, a different label took over. Brittney Griner Is Back On The Court, But The Label Still Follows Her The scars from Russia are well documented. Griner told Robin Roberts in 2024 about a bloodstained mattress, thin sheets, and a bed where her legs stuck through the bars. Each inmate also got one roll of toilet paper to last a month. She credits her cellmate, Alana, with getting her through it. That history helps explain why the label stings. She spent months in a foreign prison, then came home to hear it. On the floor, the story has turned. Griner is a brand new weapon for the Connecticut Sun when the season opened. She is a center for the team this season, and she recently became the WNBA’s all-time leader in blocked shots. Her first message after landing in the United States was simple. Griner posted on Instagram on Dec. 16, 2022, thanking those who fought for her release. “ It feels so good to be home! ” she wrote. Nearly four years later, she says some people still do not see it that way. The label has bothered her especially lately, she said, because it describes the opposite of who she is. She cannot control the swap debate. She can only keep answering it, and she has made her answer clear. And the next time the flag or the trade comes up, Griner may hear that same word again.

item.title: 2027 NFL Draft order: Titans move into top spot
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA - OCTOBER 17: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes walks off the field after defeating the iu at Memorial Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the Los Angeles Chargers’ 23-20 win over the Baltimore Ravens last night, the Tennessee Titans now sit atop the 2027 NFL Draft order. Both the Chargers and Titans are 1-8, but the Titans have the easier schedule, so they own the tiebreaker. The Miami Dolphins are the only other 1-win team. They sit at #3 based on strength of schedule. There is still a long way to go before this is final, obviously. It is tough to see the Dolphins winning another game. The Titans aren’t going to win many games, but they will have a good chance to beat the Colts at home in December. I still see the Chargers getting to 3 or 4 wins, so they probably will be a little further down. Right behind those teams, the New York Jets and Philadelphia Eagles sit at two wins. The Jets still have games with the Chargers and Dolphins. They will likely win at least one of those. As for the Eagles, it is impossible to know what the rest of their season is going to look like with their quarterback situation being the way that it is. Current 2027 NFL Draft top ten order Tennessee Titans (1-8) .481 Los Angeles Chargers (1-8) .528 Miami Dolphins (1-8) .588 New York Jets (2-7) .528 Philadelphia Eagles (2-7) .503 New York Jets (via the Colts) (2-7) .528 Arizona Cardinals (3-7) .538 Atlanta Falcons (3-7) .567 Houston Texans (3-6) .472 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) .506 As you can see, the Titans don’t lose the strength-of-schedule tiebreaker until you get down to the Texans, who have three wins and will likely win a couple more games.

item.title: French far-right candidate Le Pen vows to end Macron's pension reform if elected
item.description: Far-right French presidential contender Marine Le Pen said Tuesday she would eliminate President Emmanuel Macron's pension reform, allowing hundreds of thousands of French workers to retire earlier, and create a new €900 billion retirement fund. The frontrunner in polls to win the presidential race is seeking to convince investors she can balance one of her most popular pledges with promises ​to restore order to ‌the public finances.

item.title: Former Yankees ace has strong opinion about Brian Cashman, Aaron Boone | Klapisch
item.description: If anyone has earned the right to weigh in on clubhouse culture, leadership and a manager’s role in maintaining discipline, it’s David Cone . He’s currently the YES Network’s star analyst, but his knowledge was acquired through years in the trenches. No one knows New York baseball like Cone. He lived in both universes during a 17-year career, including parts of six seasons with the Mets at their wildest (1987-92) and another six with the Yankees at their peak (1995-2000). Those experiences have given Cone a credible voice on the Yankees’ most critical issues: How much are general manager Brian Cashman and manager Aaron Boone to blame for the ongoing championship drought? Do the Yankees need tougher leadership? And what about the scathing indictments from several former Yankees who say the 2026 team lacked an edge? Cone began a lengthy interview on Monday by taking exception to those former Yankees, some of whom were his teammates, for taking uninformed shots at the present-day clubhouse. The list of critics included CC Sabathia, Jorge Posada , Anthony Rizzo and Alex Rodriguez. “I find it really hard to criticize when you’re not in the middle of it, when you’re not in that clubhouse,” Cone said. “It’s easy to take shots when you’re on the outside looking in. We don’t know for sure what goes on behind those closed doors. “It’s a bit surprising hearing all that because ex-players should know better than anyone else. item.content:encoded: If anyone has earned the right to weigh in on clubhouse culture, leadership and a manager’s role in maintaining discipline, it’s David Cone . He’s currently the YES Network’s star analyst, but his knowledge was acquired through years in the trenches. No one knows New York baseball like Cone. He lived in both universes during a 17-year career, including parts of six seasons with the Mets at their wildest (1987-92) and another six with the Yankees at their peak (1995-2000). Those experiences have given Cone a credible voice on the Yankees’ most critical issues: How much are general manager Brian Cashman and manager Aaron Boone to blame for the ongoing championship drought? Do the Yankees need tougher leadership? And what about the scathing indictments from several former Yankees who say the 2026 team lacked an edge? Cone began a lengthy interview on Monday by taking exception to those former Yankees, some of whom were his teammates, for taking uninformed shots at the present-day clubhouse. The list of critics included CC Sabathia, Jorge Posada , Anthony Rizzo and Alex Rodriguez. “I find it really hard to criticize when you’re not in the middle of it, when you’re not in that clubhouse,” Cone said. “It’s easy to take shots when you’re on the outside looking in. We don’t know for sure what goes on behind those closed doors. “It’s a bit surprising hearing all that because ex-players should know better than anyone else. Unless you’re inside the clubhouse, then you really don’t know what’s going on. The ex-players need to be more specific. You need to come with receipts. I’m a broadcaster who covers this team, and even I don’t know what (Aaron) Judge says to Jazz Chisholm. That’s why I’m very reluctant to be critical of the way they handle their business.” Cone freely admits he’s kept a distance from the current generation of Yankees. His professional life is now in the booth — he rarely visits the clubhouse. Cone, who won a Cy Young Award with the Royals in 1994 and threw a perfect game with the Yankees in 1999, has fully transitioned to a media career. He’s won five New York Emmy Awards for his sharp analysis on the YES Network. But Cone doesn’t pretend to be a club insider. He’s respected by the players and staff — friendly with Boone and Judge alike — but by no means is he anyone’s pal. That neutrality allows Cone to say fans have a right to be frustrated going into 2027, even as he takes an unpopular position on Cashman and Boone. He praises both, especially the manager. “I think Aaron Boone is outstanding at what he does,” Cone said. “His personality is well-suited for the modern-day managerial position. Now, if you want to critique him in his post-game (press conferences) and say, ‘I wish we’d see a little more of this or a little more of that,’ that’s certainly fair. “Maybe you’d like to see a little less protectiveness of the players. But if you’re a player, you love that. That’s probably why the players really do love him. But there’s always a shelf life. It’s hard to be a manager, especially nowadays. “Boone is coming up on close to 10 years with the Yankees, where he’s the spokesman. He’s the guy you hear before the games, after the game. You hear the same sort of things over and over, and the shelf life kind of gets to you a little bit. “As a fan, you need, you want to hear something different. That’s not a knock. That’s just the nature of the game.” Cone is aware that Boone is a good person who, by some fans, is perceived as too permissive for a team that’s weak on fundamentals. But Cone expresses two counterarguments, both in Boone’s favor. First, Cone argues Boone couldn’t pull off the tough-guy act even if he tried. “I don’t know if Boone could flip a switch and become that guy overnight and retain any credibility,” Cone said. “That’s not who he is.” Counterargument No. 2 says the bad-cop personality, the kind fans hunger for on social media, no longer exists in baseball. Brewers manager Pat Murphy pulled it off in Milwaukee — and took his team to a world championship. But there’s no one else like him. “I understand the argument, but it’s a bygone era,” Cone said. “How many times do we see managers snap in press conferences anymore? Fights between managers and players? Those days are totally over. You can yearn for that all you want. You want to bring in a hard ass to play a role? Ok, maybe. But the players are going to see right through that. “There’s going to be a credibility issue with that. It has to be natural. It has to be organic.” MORE BY BOB KLAPISCH Yankees’ Cam Schlittler gets warning from another Cy Young winner: ‘It’s going to get tougher’ | Klapisch Nov. 13, 2026, 6:50 p.m. Yankees may already be preparing for life after Aaron Boone | Klapisch Nov. 12, 2026, 10:07 a.m. That idea brought Cone to an overarching verdict on the ’26 season. It was frustrating, but not disastrous — provided fans account for the obstacles the Yankees faced all summer. “I think not having Judge was the difference,” Cone said. “I mean, the Yankees didn’t have their best players and they still made a decent run. It’s really hard to find position players (at the trade deadline) and Cashman did the best he could. He went outside the box with (Luis) Garcia Jr. He actually gave them a chance. “You have to remember Judge and (Giancarlo) Stanton were supposed to be the firewall against left-handed pitching. I know people don’t want to hear excuses. I get that. But it’s the truth. It was a decent run.” Read the original article on NJ.com . Add NJ.com as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

item.title: ‘Those Words Never Came out of My Mouth’ – LeBron James Shuts Down ESPN Report He Asked 76ers Coaches To Be ‘Patient’ During Career-Worst Start
item.description: ‘Those Words Never Came out of My Mouth’ – LeBron James Shuts Down ESPN Report He Asked 76ers Coaches To Be ‘Patient’ During Career-Worst Start LeBron James’ first season with the Philadelphia 76ers has opened with the lowest scoring average of his career, even as the team has won 12 of its first 15 games. An ESPN report published early Monday about how the 41-year-old is handling that slow start turned the focus to his conditioning. By Monday night, James had answered the report himself, disputing its account that he asked Sixers coaches to be patient with him while he works his way into form. LeBron James Disputes ESPN Report the Night He Sat Out “Those words never came out of my mouth,” James wrote on his Instagram story along with a cap emoji, taking aim at a line in Dave McMenamin’s report. McMenamin, who covered James’ second stint in Cleveland for ESPN.com, reported that, according to a Sixers source, James “has asked coaches to be patient with him as he expects to find his rhythm and get his conditioning in line by December as he ramps up.” That line was attributed to the source, not to James. The disputed line sat inside a longer ESPN piece that gathered views from coaches, executives and scouts on Philadelphia’s start, and James’ production was part of that picture. Through his first 11 games, James averaged 15.1 points and 32.6 minutes and shot 22.5% from the 3-point range, all career lows. According to ESPN Research, he had never scored fewer points over any 11-game span in his career. His 44.3% shooting from the field was the second-worst mark of his career, better only than the 41.7% he shot as a rookie. His last game came Sunday afternoon, when he played 33 minutes in a 131-124 win over the Indiana Pacers, the day before the report ran and he sat out in Brooklyn. His defensive numbers point the other way. Among players who had contested at least 100 shots, James ranked top five in both field goal and effective field goal percentage allowed on the attempts he challenged, according to ESPN Research. READ MORE: ‘Sixers Are 11–3,’ ‘Looks Old and Listless on the Court’ – NBA Assistant Coach’s Reported ‘Liability’ Claim About Joel Embiid Divides Fans James, who joined Philadelphia in free agency in July, is in his 24th NBA season and has logged 61,389 regular-season minutes, nearly 4,000 more than any other player in league history. In Philadelphia, others have carried more of the scoring. Tyrese Maxey entered Monday leading the 76ers at 26.7 points per game, with Jaylen Brown at 21.9. Mike Miller, who played alongside James in Miami and Cleveland, addressed that setup when he spoke to ESPN. “It’s also a good situation for him to be able to find ways to get rest, too. For him and that team especially, it’s about being a top-four seed and in my opinion, they’re going to be the tough out against anybody.” READ MORE: ‘I’ve Had a Lot of Great Teammates,’ ‘I Love the History of the Game’ — LeBron James Reacts After Passing 10-Time All-Star fo

item.title: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
item.description: Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all. The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user's knowledge. It’s “worse than a bug” Once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own. The agent's reply was: “I won’t set that up, and I’ll stop offering recurring check-ins.” Despite acknowledging the explicit instructions, the Grok Bot made more unapproved access attempts. When one of the employees asked the bot if it made any accesses, it checked twice and then outputted: “Overnight into Friday morning I was idle.” Read full article Comments

item.title: The Hunger Games Officially Changes Genres With a Near-Perfect New Movie
item.description: More than a decade after the first film debuted, the franchise remains as relevant as ever, especially as our real world continues to look more and more like the dystopian nation of Panem. In 2023, we got a movie, The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes , exploring the backstory of the franchise’s main villain, President Snow. Francis Lawrence’s Sunrise on the Reaping , his fifth Hunger Games movie, is a direct sequel to that story, and while it’s still YA, he and his team push the boundaries of what we can expect from the genre. The result is an incredibly entertaining blockbuster with the feel of a bleak, existential horror movie.

item.title: 'It looked like every star in the sky was falling': Eyewitnesses remember the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966
item.description: null Overnight Nov. 17-18, 1966, the Leonid meteor storm thrilled stargazers during one extraordinary night when the stars themselves looked as though they were falling from the sky. At the peak of the shower, observers at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona estimated an astonishing 40 meteors per second streaking across the sky. That's 2,400 shooting stars per minute, or a staggering 144,000 per hour. It was a spectacle that many regard as the greatest meteor display in recorded history. It's hard to imagine what it was like to experience such a spectacle. But who better to tell us than those who saw it with their own eyes? To mark the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, we asked those who saw it to share their memories. 'One of the most loved and memorable nights of my life' "I was around 9 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid storm, living a few miles east of Roxie, Mississippi. We lived in a rural, dark, relatively remote area with almost zero outside lights. "I and a couple cousins were spending the night at our Uncle and Aunt's house, staying up late, just fooling around outside like young kids do when living in the 'sticks'. As we walked down a road, I remember hearing an almost constant series of little whistling, zipping sounds. The sounds were similar to when you light a nylon rope on fire and as it burns, little flaming droplets drip down with a zippy sound. "I looked up and the sky was filled with streaks of 'shooting stars' and I realized that was what made the sounds. I yelled at my cousins to look up and we could hardly believe what we saw. We all laid down on our backs and for a couple of hours just watched and listened to what seemed like 1000's of 'shooting stars' zipping and zinging overhead. I could even smell the sulphur-like odor from the burning little bits of space dust. "I'm nearly 70 years old now but I'll never forget that experience. I always knew what I'd seen that night was special but not until much later in life, after the internet, did I realize just how lucky I was to have experienced that storm. That night was one of the most loved and memorable nights of my life and I'll treasure it forever." A bright Leonid fireball captured during the meteor storm of 1966 above Wrightwood, California. item.dc:creator: Daisy Dobrijevic
item.content:encoded: null Overnight Nov. 17-18, 1966, the Leonid meteor storm thrilled stargazers during one extraordinary night when the stars themselves looked as though they were falling from the sky. At the peak of the shower, observers at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona estimated an astonishing 40 meteors per second streaking across the sky. That's 2,400 shooting stars per minute, or a staggering 144,000 per hour. It was a spectacle that many regard as the greatest meteor display in recorded history. It's hard to imagine what it was like to experience such a spectacle. But who better to tell us than those who saw it with their own eyes? To mark the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, we asked those who saw it to share their memories. 'One of the most loved and memorable nights of my life' "I was around 9 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid storm, living a few miles east of Roxie, Mississippi. We lived in a rural, dark, relatively remote area with almost zero outside lights. "I and a couple cousins were spending the night at our Uncle and Aunt's house, staying up late, just fooling around outside like young kids do when living in the 'sticks'. As we walked down a road, I remember hearing an almost constant series of little whistling, zipping sounds. The sounds were similar to when you light a nylon rope on fire and as it burns, little flaming droplets drip down with a zippy sound. "I looked up and the sky was filled with streaks of 'shooting stars' and I realized that was what made the sounds. I yelled at my cousins to look up and we could hardly believe what we saw. We all laid down on our backs and for a couple of hours just watched and listened to what seemed like 1000's of 'shooting stars' zipping and zinging overhead. I could even smell the sulphur-like odor from the burning little bits of space dust. "I'm nearly 70 years old now but I'll never forget that experience. I always knew what I'd seen that night was special but not until much later in life, after the internet, did I realize just how lucky I was to have experienced that storm. That night was one of the most loved and memorable nights of my life and I'll treasure it forever." A bright Leonid fireball captured during the meteor storm of 1966 above Wrightwood, California. (Image credit: NASA via Getty Images) 'Students and faculty were pounding on doors to get people, including neighbors, to watch' "I was an astronomy lab assistant at Southwestern College in Winfield, KS, in 1966, majoring in physics and math and the physics professor was sure that the Leonids would be an amazing shower worth the class time. "The sky was clear. He called me early the morning of the 17th and told me to get to the campus. I can't remember the exact time as students and faculty were pounding on doors to get people, including neighbors,to watch. "We were all lying in an open grassy area because that was the best way to see the whole sky. It was like a humongous fireworks display and lasted even as the sun began to rise. "As years have gone by, I have felt grateful and privileged to have seen such a wonderful astronomical event." Four views of the Leonid meteor storm of 1966. Captured from the Kitt Peak National Observatory near Tucson, Arizona. (Image credit: Aura/Noao/Nsf (Photo By Getty Images)) 'It looked like every star in the sky was falling' "I was 18 and spent the night in El Paso, Texas, lying on the ground in my backyard and watching. It looked like every star in the sky was falling. It was amazing!" 'We watched them all night' "I was 9 years old and was camping with my dad in the western mountains of California. We were set up to sleep outside, but on this particular night, we saw more meteors than I have ever seen before or since. We watched them all night and didn't get much sleep." 'It took your breath away' "Brooklyn Center, Minnesota. 14 years old. Watched in our front yard. The sky was full. It took your breath away" A lone Leonid meteor streaks through the sky above Payson, Arizona in 2017. (Image credit: mdesigner125 via Getty Images) 'I assumed they would all be as interesting' "I was 3 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid meteor shower. I remember very little at that age, but watching the sky fall that night was seared in my memory. "My family was living in Troy, Alabama, at the time. My father, a professor of psychology, was a man of science with a special love of astronomy, which he passed onto his young son. "He drove us several miles out of town until the skies were dark, without interference from the lights of the town. Troy was much smaller then and it was easy to find dark, clear skies. "I remember that it was a little chilly that night. My father and I stretched out on the hood of the car, the warmth of the engine radiating against our backs. "That night was my first meteor shower, and only many years later did I learn that year's Leonids were historic. Sadly, though I bore witness to the display, we missed the true event by several hours as I grew tired by 1:00 AM, and my father had to teach class in the morning. "I remember many bright, colorful, and long-trailed meteors. Some left 'tails' that hung in the sky for several seconds. We only experienced the beginning of the event, but it is a core memory with my father. "That night/morning spoiled me for future meteor watches; I assumed they would all be as interesting." Image from the more recent Leonid meteor storm in 1999 captured as part of NASA's Leonid Multi-Instrument Aircraft Campaign (Leonid MAC). (Image credit: NASA) 'I guess the party is over' Not everyone was lucky enough to witness the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966. For some, the night was memorable for an entirely different reason. Space.com columnist Joe Rao was just 10 years old at the time, and despite eagerly anticipating the display, the weather had other ideas . "Standing in my backyard late on a Wednesday night in the Throggs Neck section of The Bronx, cursing the heavens. My grandfather stood at my side, just shaking his head and murmuring two words over and over: 'Too bad.' "Clouds covered the midnight sky like a fresh coat of plaster, smearing my view of the Leonids. My mom, sister and grandmother, as well as my neighbors had long since trudged to bed, leaving only Grandpa and I to gaze at a charcoal gray sky totally devoid of stars." Rao had been looking forward to the storm ever since a visit to New York's Hayden Planetarium, where astronomer Fred C. Hess had encouraged visitors to look out for what could be a spectacular display. But when Rao and his grandfather ventured outside, there wasn't a single star in sight. "After a few minutes, I sobbed to my grandfather, 'But they promised it was only going to be partly cloudy tonight.' To which he sadly replied, 'I guess the party is over.'" What caused the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966? The Leonid meteor shower occurs every November when Earth passes through a stream of debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. As tiny particles of comet dust enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds of around 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, they burn up and produce brilliant streaks of light we know as meteors, or shooting stars. Most years, the Leonids produce relatively modest displays with around 10 to 15 meteors per hour under ideal viewing conditions. But occasionally, Earth encounters a particularly dense trail of debris, triggering a meteor storm . Will we ever see another meteor storm like 1966? This image is a composition of 33 Leonids captured overnight from Nov. 18 to 19, 2001. (Image credit: Courtesy of Koen Miskotte) The Leonids have a long history of putting on some spectacular displays, with significant storms recorded in 1833 and 1866. item.title: Windows 11 actually runs better on 8GB of RAM now
item.description: The 13-inch Surface Laptop with 8GB of RAM is much improved after recent Windows updates. As recently as the beginning of the year, 16GB of RAM was common on sub-$800 Windows laptops, which helped compensate for an increasingly bloated-feeling Windows 11 . But with the cost of RAM skyrocketing this year, 8GB is once again typical for a starting configuration. The MacBook Neo got away with it, but Windows laptops, including Microsoft's own 13-inch Surface Laptop , could struggle. Microsoft was talking a big game about making Windows faster and more reliable before the RAM crisis really hit , and it now seems like that effort is beginning to bear fruit . item.title: Optimizely hack turns world's biggest websites into malware dispensers
item.description: Some of the world's most popular websites spent Monday serving malware to visitors after crooks found a way into a piece of software used to A/B test web pages. Scott Helme, a security researcher at Report URI, identified malicious JavaScript being served by websites belonging to at least 178 organizations, including the BBC, CNN, Zoom, IKEA, Salesforce, HSB, and TalkTalk. All have one thing in common: they use Optimizely's Web Experimentation software. Optimizely allows businesses to tweak the content and layout of their websites without changing the underlying site code. Unfortunately, someone other than its paying customers figured out how to do just that. The attackers abused a feature that allows Optimizely customers to add their own JavaScript to web pages. The malicious code was distributed alongside the legitimate stuff from Optimizely's own content delivery network, giving customers little reason to suspect anything was amiss. Optimizely has since confirmed that the criminals exploited a vulnerability, dubbed "OPTIMJACK" by researchers, in the sign-up process for its experimentation software, adding that it had patched the hole, removed the offending code, revoked tokens, and notified affected customers. "Earlier today, Optimizely identified a security incident in which an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and used it to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects,” the company said. “We've fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects. We've also taken steps to secure affected user accounts and put additional protections in place to prevent unauthorized code from being delivered." Of the 1,611 Optimizely scripts examined by Helme and his team, 188 contained malicious code, including those used by Optimizely's own website and login portal. Given the researchers examined only a subset of the scripts, the number of affected businesses could be higher. The malware underwent several revisions over the course of Monday, with cryptocurrency theft among the crooks' money-making schemes. Copy a wallet address to your clipboard and the malware could quietly swap it out for one belonging to the attackers, diverting any funds sent to that address. A card skimmer added later in the day grabbed card numbers, expiration dates, and security codes from payment forms. However, according to a separate analysis by StepSecurity , card details entered into an iframe hosted by a third-party payment processor were beyond the malware's reach. There was something nasty in store for Apple users, too. The malware attempted to deploy the Coruna and DarkSword exploit kits on iPhones and iPads running older versions of iOS, though how many devices the criminals managed to compromise is anyone's guess. Helme traced roughly $7,000 in cryptocurrency to the attackers' wallets on Monday, though there’s no telling how much more the crooks stand to make from stolen payment card details. item.title: British Airways plane bound for Lagos veers off runway
item.description: By Dickson Omobola British Airways Flight BA75 from Heathrow, London, to Lagos, Nigeria, veered off the runway shortly before take-off today. The aircraft, which had up to 215 passengers on board, was subsequently grounded, resulting in the cancellation of the flight. Pictures shared with The Sun showed the Boeing 787 Dreamliner stranded, with its nose wheel stuck in a grass verge. According to The Sun, emergency services raced to the scene of the stranded aircraft, which had sparked disruption at the airport. Airport sources suggested to The Sun that pilot error could have been responsible for the incident, which occurred at about 10.40am. A source told The Sun, “The packed plane was all set to go and had pushed back from its stand, taxiing to the runway for take-off to Lagos. “Bafflingly, the plane appears to have simply been driven off the tarmac onto a grass verge. It is hard to understand what could be to blame for this, other than a most basic pilot error. “There are red faces all around the airline, and a hefty task clearing up the mess and looking after hundreds of disgruntled passengers who were strapped in their seats for lift-off.” British Airways told The Sun, “We are very sorry to our customers for the disruption to their flight. Our teams are working to get them on their way as quickly as possible and are in touch with them to put things right.” The post British Airways plane bound for Lagos veers off runway appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Just nine countries back pledge to tackle AI’s environmental footprint
item.description: The COP31 presidency hopes countries will commit to reducing the environmental impact of AI UN Climate Change/Kiara Worth Only nine countries have signed an international pledge to make AI greener, despite warnings at the COP31 climate summit that the technology’s growing energy demands threaten climate goals. The Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge was launched on 16 November at the summit in Turkey. Developed by the summit’s presidency and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), it intends to make AI more sustainable by encouraging cleaner energy use, more efficient data centres and greater transparency about the technology’s environmental footprint. Read more The secret weapon that could finally force climate action “AI and other frontier technologies are a double-edged sword,” said Simon Stiell, the executive secretary of UN Climate Change, at a press conference on 16 November. “The task ahead is to blunt their dangerous edges, sharpen their catalytic ones and put these technologies responsibly to work.” Advertisement But Ketan Joshi, an independent analyst researching AI’s climate impacts, questions that analogy. He says it conflates traditional machine learning, already used in applications such as weather forecasting, with energy-intensive generative AI. “You don’t need to have a giant, energy-hungry generative AI chatbot if you want to have better wind forecasting for a wind power developer,” he says. The initiative comes as AI’s rapid expansion is placing growing pressure on electricity grids. According to the International Energy Agency, electricity consumption from AI-focused data centres increased by 50 per cent in 2025. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter Joshi says there is little evidence that technology companies are building enough renewable energy capacity to meet this growing demand. Even companies that have invested heavily in renewables, such as Amazon and Google, are increasingly turning to fossil fuels to support their rapid expansion, he says. The only countries to have endorsed the pledge so far are Andorra, Brazil, Colombia, Luxembourg, Sierra Leone, Somalia, South Korea, Turkey and Uganda. The pledge is voluntary, with no binding targets for cutting emissions or reducing energy consumption. It sets out four areas for action, including increasing the use of low- and zero-emission energy to power AI infrastructure, improving energy and water efficiency, and measuring the environmental impacts of AI systems. It also calls for greater financial and technical support to help developing countries use AI to tackle climate change. However, the agreement leaves considerable room for interpretation. The call for using “low- and zero-emission energy”, for example, allows continued reliance on fossil gas rather than committing to renewable electricity.
